Text 2: Standardized tests measure only a narrow range of skills and disadvantage students from lower-income backgrounds who have less access to test preparation. They also create incentives for 'teaching to the test,' crowding out richer learning experiences.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 that standardized tests reliably measure student learning?
fields.option_a: Standardized tests do reliably measure learning, but only for students in well-funded schools.
fields.option_b: The tests' narrow focus and socioeconomic bias undermine their reliability as a fair measure of learning.
fields.option_c: Policymakers should eliminate all forms of student assessment.
fields.option_d: Standardized tests are not useful for any educational purpose.
fields.explanation: Text 2 argues that the tests measure narrow skills and disadvantage lower-income students — both points challenge the claim of reliable, objective measurement.

fields.text:
Scientists studying ancient Egyptian mummies have used CT scans and DNA analysis to determine causes of death for individuals who lived more than 3,000 years ago. One study found evidence of ________ in arterial walls of several mummies, suggesting that cardiovascular disease is not solely a modern phenomenon.

Which choice most effectively completes the claim using evidence consistent with the rest of the text?
fields.explanation: Calcification (hardening) of arterial walls is a marker of atherosclerosis — cardiovascular disease — which is exactly what the sentence is claiming to find.

fields.text:
A study surveyed 500 participants about their primary mode of transportation:

Car: 285 | Public Transit: 115 | Bicycle: 60 | Walking: 40

A researcher states that car travel accounts for more than half of all reported modes. Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support this claim?
fields.option_a: Bicycle use (60) and walking (40) together represent 20% of respondents.
fields.option_b: Car travel was chosen by 285 of 500 respondents, which is 57% — more than half.
fields.option_c: Public transit (115) is the second most common mode after car.
fields.option_d: Walking is the least common mode of transportation among respondents.
fields.explanation: 285/500 = 57%, which is more than half. Option B directly calculates the percentage to support the claim.

fields.text:
Text 1: Historical records show that Easter Island's population collapsed before European contact, attributed to unsustainable exploitation of forest resources. This 'ecocide' is widely taught as an example of environmental self-destruction.

Text 2: Archaeological evidence increasingly suggests the population collapse was primarily caused by European-introduced diseases and slave raids, not prior ecological devastation. Pollen data shows deforestation happened gradually over centuries, not in the sudden manner that a catastrophic collapse would require.

Based on the texts, the authors disagree about which of the following?
fields.option_a: Whether Europeans ever made contact with Easter Island's inhabitants.
fields.option_b: Whether Easter Island's population declined significantly at some point.
fields.option_c: The primary cause of Easter Island's population decline.
fields.option_d: Whether deforestation occurred at all on Easter Island.
fields.explanation: Text 1 attributes the collapse to ecological self-destruction; Text 2 attributes it to European diseases and slave raids — they disagree on the primary cause.

fields.text:
The university's new policies, which aim to improve student wellness and increase retention rates, ________ expected to take effect at the beginning of the next academic year.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: The plural subject 'policies' requires the plural verb 'are.'

fields.text:
The renowned chef, who trained under several Michelin-starred masters in Paris, ________ her first solo restaurant in 2019 to widespread critical acclaim.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: 'Opened' is the correct simple past tense — the action occurred 'in 2019.'

fields.text:
________ the first complete map of the human genome, scientists gained unprecedented insight into the genetic basis of thousands of diseases.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: 'Having completed' is the correct perfect participial phrase, indicating the prior action that enabled the subsequent scientific gains.

fields.text:
Neither the director nor the principal actor ________ aware of the technical problems with the sound equipment until the premiere screening.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: With 'neither...nor,' the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Principal actor' is singular → 'was.'

fields.text:
The researcher identified three key factors contributing to chronic workplace stress ________ excessive workload, lack of task autonomy, and poor communication with supervisors.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: A colon correctly introduces the list of three factors that follows.

fields.text:
The ancient library at Alexandria was among the greatest repositories of knowledge in antiquity ________ scholars from across the Mediterranean traveled there to access its vast collection of scrolls.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.

fields.text:
The newly discovered species ________ named Cryodrakon boreas — was the largest flying animal ever found in Canada, with a wingspan estimated at over 30 feet.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: The parenthetical 'named Cryodrakon boreas' is set off by dashes. Since the closing dash is present, the opening punctuation must also be a dash.

fields.text:
The ancient manuscript was discovered in a cave near the Dead Sea in 1947 ________ becoming one of the most significant archaeological finds of the twentieth century.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: A comma introduces the participial phrase 'becoming one of the most significant...' that modifies the discovery.

fields.text:
Photosynthesis requires sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to produce glucose and oxygen. ________ the process can be disrupted by prolonged cloud cover or air pollution, which reduces the sunlight available to plants.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
fields.explanation: 'However' introduces a contrasting limitation — despite the requirements described, the process can be disrupted.

fields.text:
Researchers at the university spent three years developing a new water purification system. ________ the system can now remove 99% of common contaminants from drinking water at a fraction of the traditional cost.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
fields.explanation: 'As a result' connects the years of research to the successful outcome — cause and effect.

fields.text:
Many species of migratory birds navigate using Earth's magnetic field, which they sense through specialized proteins in their eyes. ________ some birds also use the positions of stars and the angle of the sun to navigate.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
fields.explanation: 'In addition' correctly signals that the text is adding another navigation method used by migratory birds.

fields.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Amazon River is the world's largest river by discharge volume, releasing approximately 20% of all freshwater entering the world's oceans.
- It flows approximately 3,976 miles from its source in Peru to its mouth in Brazil.
- The Amazon basin is home to approximately 10% of all species on Earth.
- The river supports over 30 million people, including hundreds of indigenous communities.
- Scientists estimate the Amazon rainforest produces about 6% of Earth's oxygen.

The student wants to emphasize the Amazon's significance for biodiversity. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
fields.option_a: The Amazon flows 3,976 miles and releases 20% of all freshwater entering the oceans.
fields.option_b: The Amazon basin is home to approximately 10% of all species on Earth, making it one of the planet's most biodiverse regions.
fields.option_c: The Amazon River supports over 30 million people, including hundreds of indigenous communities.
fields.option_d: The Amazon rainforest produces about 6% of Earth's oxygen.
fields.explanation: Option B directly addresses biodiversity — 10% of all Earth's species — which is the student's stated goal.

fields.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Wright Brothers' first powered flight was on December 17, 1903, at Kitty Hawk, NC.
- The first flight lasted 12 seconds and covered 120 feet.
- Later that same day, a flight lasted 59 seconds and covered 852 feet.
- Today, commercial aircraft travel at over 500 mph and carry hundreds of passengers.

The student wants to show the dramatic progress in aviation. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
fields.option_a: The Wright Brothers' flight at Kitty Hawk lasted 12 seconds and covered 120 feet.
fields.option_b: On the same day, the Wright Brothers achieved a flight of 59 seconds covering 852 feet.
fields.option_c: The Wright Brothers' first flight occurred on December 17, 1903, at Kitty Hawk.
fields.option_d: Compared to the Wright Brothers' first 12-second, 120-foot flight, modern commercial aircraft fly at over 500 mph and carry hundreds of passengers.
fields.explanation: Option D creates a direct comparison across time — the tiny first flight versus today's massive commercial aircraft — which best demonstrates dramatic progress.

fields.text:
The library's new reading program has been very popular. Students ________ books from many different genres, discovering new interests along the way.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Explore' logically fits — students are discovering new interests through reading across genres.

fields.text:
The volunteer firefighters responded quickly to the emergency. Their ________ efforts saved the historic building from complete destruction.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Heroic' describes brave, courageous effort — fitting for firefighters who saved a building.

fields.text:
Scientists made an exciting discovery when they found fossils of a previously unknown dinosaur species in Montana. The dinosaur is believed to be a ________ predator that lived about 75 million years ago.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Fierce' means aggressive and powerful — fitting for a predatory dinosaur. ('Extinct' would apply to all ancient dinosaurs and is too vague.)

fields.text:
The school's new recycling program has been a great success. Students are ________ the program by separating their waste into the correct bins each day.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Supporting' means helping or backing up — fitting for students who participate actively in the recycling program.

fields.text:
Penguins are found almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere, with most species living in Antarctica and surrounding islands. Though often associated with ice and snow, some penguin species actually live in temperate or even subtropical climates, including the Galapagos penguin, which lives near the equator.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
fields.option_a: Penguins can only survive in extremely cold climates near Antarctica.
fields.option_b: Penguins are found in the Southern Hemisphere, but some species live in surprisingly warm climates.
fields.option_c: The Galapagos penguin is the most common penguin species in the world.
fields.option_d: Scientists do not fully understand why penguins live in the Southern Hemisphere.
fields.explanation: The text explains where penguins live and notes the surprising fact that some live in warm climates — the main idea.

fields.text:
The printing press, invented by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440, transformed European society by making books affordable and widely available. Before the printing press, books were copied by hand, a slow and expensive process that limited access to knowledge. Within 50 years of Gutenberg's invention, millions of books had been printed across Europe.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
fields.option_a: Johannes Gutenberg invented the printing press to make money from book sales.
fields.option_b: Books became worthless after the printing press was invented because so many were produced.
fields.option_c: The printing press transformed access to knowledge by making books affordable and widely available.
fields.option_d: Before Gutenberg, only monks were allowed to copy books by hand.
fields.explanation: The main idea is how the printing press changed book availability and access to knowledge.

fields.text:
Rainforests cover only about 6% of Earth's surface but are home to more than half of the world's plant and animal species. They also play a critical role in regulating the climate by absorbing carbon dioxide and producing oxygen. Despite their importance, rainforests continue to be cleared for agriculture and development.

Which choice best describes the function of the last sentence in the text?
fields.option_a: It explains why rainforests are home to so many species.
fields.option_b: It introduces a concern that contrasts with the rainforest's established importance.
fields.option_c: It suggests that agriculture is more important than rainforest conservation.
fields.option_d: It provides details about how carbon dioxide affects rainforests.
fields.explanation: After explaining the rainforest's importance, the final sentence introduces the contrasting problem of continued deforestation.

fields.text:
In ancient Rome, the Forum was the center of public life. Citizens gathered there to conduct business, watch speeches, and participate in civic ceremonies. The Forum contained temples, government buildings, and market stalls, making it a hub for religion, politics, and commerce.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
fields.option_a: The Roman Forum was mainly used for religious ceremonies.
fields.option_b: The Forum was the center of Roman public life, combining commercial, political, and religious functions.
fields.option_c: Only wealthy Roman citizens were allowed to enter the Forum.
fields.option_d: The Roman Forum was primarily a marketplace where merchants sold goods.
fields.explanation: The text describes the Forum as central to all aspects of Roman public life — religion, politics, and commerce.

fields.text:
Scientists at NASA have been studying the possibility of growing food on Mars. Plants need sunlight, water, and nutrients to grow, all of which present challenges on Mars. However, researchers have found that certain crops, such as potatoes and radishes, could potentially grow in Martian soil with modifications. This finding ________

Which choice most logically completes the text?
fields.option_a: proves that humans could never survive on Mars.
fields.option_b: suggests that long-term human habitation on Mars may be more feasible than previously thought.
fields.option_c: shows that potatoes are the only viable food source in space.
fields.option_d: indicates that Martian soil is identical to soil found on Earth.
fields.explanation: If some crops could grow on Mars, this makes long-term human habitation more plausible — the logical completion of the text.

fields.text:
The table below shows the number of students participating in after-school clubs:

Drama: 24 | Science: 18 | Art: 30 | Chess: 12 | Sports: 36

A teacher claims that Art and Drama together attract more students than Sports. Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to evaluate this claim?
fields.option_a: Art (30) is the second-most popular club after Sports (36).
fields.option_b: Art (30) + Drama (24) = 54, which is greater than Sports (36). The claim is correct.
fields.option_c: Chess (12) is the least popular club.
fields.option_d: Science (18) has more participants than Chess (12).
fields.explanation: 30 + 24 = 54 > 36. Option B directly evaluates the claim using the data.

fields.text:
Text 1: Zoos play an important role in conservation by protecting endangered species, funding research, and educating the public about wildlife.

Text 2: Critics argue that keeping animals in captivity causes psychological harm and that zoos prioritize entertainment over animal welfare. Many species breed poorly in captivity and cannot be successfully released into the wild.

Based on the texts, both authors would likely agree that ________
fields.option_b: all animals in zoos can be successfully reintroduced to the wild.
fields.option_c: zoos affect wildlife in some way, but whether that effect is positive is debated.
fields.option_d: zoos are the most effective conservation strategy available.
fields.explanation: Text 1 sees zoos as beneficial; Text 2 sees them as harmful. Both agree zoos affect wildlife — they disagree on whether the effect is positive.

fields.text:
The table shows average test scores by study method:

Studying alone: 72 | Study groups: 81 | Tutoring: 88 | Online videos: 77

A student claims that using a tutor leads to the highest test scores. Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support this claim?
fields.option_a: Students who study alone score 72, which is the lowest of all methods.
fields.option_b: Tutoring (88) results in the highest average test score of the four methods listed.
fields.option_c: Study groups (81) score higher than studying alone (72) or watching online videos (77).
fields.option_d: Online video scores (77) fall between studying alone and study groups.
fields.explanation: Tutoring at 88 is higher than all other methods (72, 81, 77). Option B directly supports the claim.

fields.text:
Text 1: Breakfast is the most important meal of the day. Eating a nutritious morning meal improves concentration, stabilizes energy levels, and supports healthy metabolism.

Text 2: While breakfast can be beneficial for some people, recent research suggests it is not universally important. Some individuals perform equally well when skipping breakfast, particularly those who practice intermittent fasting.

Based on the texts, the authors would most likely agree that ________
fields.option_a: skipping breakfast always leads to poor concentration and low energy.
fields.option_b: breakfast is harmful to people who practice intermittent fasting.
fields.option_c: whether breakfast is beneficial may depend on individual differences.
fields.option_d: breakfast should be the largest meal of the day.
fields.explanation: Text 1 says breakfast is essential; Text 2 says it depends on the person. Both implicitly acknowledge individual variation.

fields.text:
The table shows the number of books borrowed from a school library per month:

September: 145 | October: 162 | November: 178 | December: 89 | January: 201

A librarian notes that book borrowing was higher in every month except December. Which choice best uses data from the table to support this observation?
fields.option_a: September had 145 borrowings, which is the lowest month except for December.
fields.option_b: October and November both saw increases over September.
fields.option_c: All months except December (89) had more than 140 borrowings, while December had the fewest.
fields.option_d: January (201) had the highest number of borrowings of any month.
fields.explanation: Option C uses the data to show all months exceeded 140 except December (89), directly supporting the librarian's observation.

fields.text:
The birds in the sanctuary ________ every morning just after sunrise, filling the air with a rich variety of songs.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: 'Birds' is plural and requires the plural verb 'sing.'

fields.text:
Last summer, the community garden ________ more than 500 pounds of vegetables, which were donated to local food banks.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: 'Produced' is the correct simple past tense — the action occurred 'last summer.'

fields.text:
The principal ________ the students for their outstanding performance at the regional science fair, where they won three first-place awards.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: 'Congratulated' is the correct simple past tense, consistent with the completed event at the science fair.

fields.text:
Every one of the volunteers ________ asked to wear a reflective vest during the outdoor event for safety reasons.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: 'Every one' is singular and takes a singular verb: 'was.'

fields.text:
The science fair had three categories of projects ________ biology, chemistry, and physics.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: A colon introduces the list of three categories that follows.

fields.text:
The students worked hard on the project all week ________ they presented their results to the class on Friday.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.

fields.text:
The school's new principal, ________ has twenty years of experience in education, started her first day with a schoolwide assembly.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: 'Who' is the correct relative pronoun for a person and is used as the subject of 'has.'

fields.text:
We explored the tide pools at the beach ________ we discovered dozens of sea stars, hermit crabs, and colorful anemones.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: A comma before the relative adverb 'where' correctly introduces a relative clause describing the beach.

fields.text:
The team practiced every afternoon for six weeks. ________ they won the regional championship by a wide margin.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
fields.explanation: 'Ultimately' signals the final result of the extended preparation — winning the championship.

fields.text:
The new park has beautiful walking trails and a large playground. ________ it also features a community garden where residents can grow their own vegetables.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
fields.explanation: 'In addition' correctly adds another feature of the park to those already mentioned.

fields.text:
The hurricane caused significant damage to coastal neighborhoods. ________ emergency services responded quickly, providing shelter and supplies to thousands of displaced residents.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
fields.explanation: 'Nevertheless' introduces the positive response despite the damage — a contrast with the difficulty of the situation.

fields.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Monarch butterflies migrate up to 3,000 miles between Canada/the US and Mexico.
- They navigate using a combination of the sun's position and Earth's magnetic field.
- A single monarch lives only a few months, yet the journey is completed over generations.
- Monarch populations have declined by more than 80% since the 1980s.
- Milkweed, the only plant monarchs breed on, has been greatly reduced by herbicide use.

The student wants to explain why monarch populations have declined. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
fields.option_a: Monarch butterflies migrate up to 3,000 miles between Canada and Mexico.
fields.option_b: A single monarch lives only a few months, yet the migration is completed across generations.
fields.option_c: Monarch populations have declined by over 80% since the 1980s, largely because milkweed — the only plant monarchs breed on — has been greatly reduced by herbicide use.
fields.option_d: Monarchs navigate using the sun and Earth's magnetic field.
fields.explanation: Option C directly explains the decline by connecting the population loss (80%) to the specific cause (milkweed reduction from herbicide use).

fields.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert in the world, covering about 9.2 million km².
- Temperatures can exceed 136°F (58°C) during the day.
- At night, temperatures can drop below freezing.
- Despite the harsh conditions, about 2 million people live there.
- The Sahara has large deposits of oil and natural gas.

The student wants to highlight the extreme temperature variation in the Sahara. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
fields.option_a: The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert, covering 9.2 million km².
fields.option_b: Despite its harsh conditions, approximately 2 million people live in the Sahara.
fields.option_c: In the Sahara, daytime temperatures can exceed 136°F while nighttime temperatures can fall below freezing.
fields.option_d: The Sahara has large deposits of oil and natural gas beneath its surface.
fields.explanation: Option C directly contrasts the extreme daytime heat (136°F) with the below-freezing nighttime cold — the most effective way to highlight temperature variation.

fields.text:
Though the critic's review of the debut novel was ultimately positive, she described the author's prose style as ________ — dense with subordinate clauses and parenthetical asides that, while intellectually rewarding, demanded considerable effort from the reader.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Labyrinthine' means complex and difficult to follow, like a maze — precisely describing prose dense with nested clauses.

fields.text:
The governor's initial response to the scandal was widely criticized as ________ — she acknowledged the problem only in the vaguest terms and declined to commit to any specific course of corrective action.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Evasive' means deliberately vague and avoiding direct answers — matching the governor's vague acknowledgment and refusal to commit.

fields.text:
Unlike historians who interpret documents cautiously, acknowledging the limits of available evidence, the author of this popular history adopts a far more ________ approach, presenting speculative reconstructions of events as established fact.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Assertive' means confidently stating things as true — contrasting with the cautious historians and matching the bold, speculative approach described.

fields.text:
The ecosystem of a coral reef is remarkably ________, with each species playing a distinct role: parrotfish graze on algae, sea urchins control coral growth, and cleaner shrimp remove parasites from fish.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Interdependent' means relying on each other — exactly describing an ecosystem where each species serves a distinct function for others.

fields.text:
The following text is adapted from Joseph Conrad's 1899 novella Heart of Darkness. Marlow, a sailor, reflects on his journey up the Congo River.

Going up that river was like traveling back to the earliest beginnings of the world, when vegetation rioted on the earth and the big trees were kings. An empty stream, a great silence, an impenetrable forest. The air was warm, thick, heavy, sluggish. There was no joy in the brilliance of sunshine.

Which choice best describes the mood conveyed by the passage?
fields.option_a: Excitement and wonder at the natural beauty of the river.
fields.option_b: A sense of oppressive, primordial heaviness and isolation.
fields.option_c: Nostalgia for a simpler, more peaceful way of life.
fields.option_d: Curiosity about the unknown plants and animals of the Congo.
fields.explanation: Conrad uses words like 'impenetrable,' 'thick,' 'heavy,' and 'no joy' to create a sense of oppression and isolation, not wonder or curiosity.

fields.text:
Neuroscientists have debated whether human creativity is localized in a specific brain region or distributed across multiple networks. Recent imaging studies suggest the latter: creative thinking involves dynamic interaction among three large-scale networks — the default mode network, the executive control network, and the salience network. The default mode generates ideas; the executive network evaluates them; the salience network determines which ideas are worth pursuing.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
fields.option_a: Creativity is located in a single, identifiable brain region.
fields.option_b: The executive control network is the most important of the three networks for creativity.
fields.option_c: Recent research suggests that creativity results from the coordinated interaction of three distinct brain networks.
fields.option_d: Neuroscientists have definitively proven that creativity cannot be studied using brain imaging.
fields.explanation: The text presents the finding that creativity involves three interacting networks — that is the main idea.

fields.text:
Sociologist Erving Goffman argued that everyday social interactions are fundamentally theatrical performances in which individuals actively manage the impressions they create. In his 'dramaturgical' model, people present a carefully curated 'front stage' self to audiences while hiding a more authentic 'backstage' self. Critics have argued that Goffman's model overstates the deliberate, calculated nature of social performance and neglects unconscious, habitual dimensions of behavior.

Based on the passage, Goffman's critics would most likely argue that his model is incomplete because it ________
fields.option_a: focuses too much on unconscious behavior rather than deliberate choices.
fields.option_b: ignores the theatrical performances that occur in formal settings.
fields.option_c: treats social behavior as more intentional than it actually is.
fields.option_d: does not adequately distinguish between front-stage and backstage selves.
fields.explanation: Critics argue Goffman overstates the deliberate, calculated nature of performance — in other words, he makes social behavior seem more intentional than it is.

fields.text:
The following text is adapted from George Eliot's 1871 novel Middlemarch. Dorothea, a young idealistic woman, reflects on her choices.

She was ashamed of being so uncertain about her own goodness; she was inclined to think she had been mistaken in supposing that she could be good to everyone. What she had supposed was a lamp to guide others had turned out to be a will-o'-the-wisp, leading herself into bogs and marshes.

Which choice best describes what the metaphor in the final sentence conveys?
fields.option_a: Dorothea believes she has become lost in an actual swamp.
fields.option_b: Dorothea feels that her idealism, which she thought would guide others, has instead misled her.
fields.option_c: Dorothea is uncertain whether she has helped anyone avoid physical danger.
fields.option_d: Dorothea has decided to abandon her effort to be good to others.
fields.explanation: The lamp-turned-will-o'-the-wisp metaphor: what she thought was guiding others has actually misled her into 'bogs and marshes' — confusion and failure.

fields.text:
Evolutionary biologist Richard Dawkins proposed that evolution acts not on organisms but on genes. In his 'selfish gene' theory, genes are the fundamental units of selection, and organisms are merely 'vehicles' through which genes propagate themselves. Critics of this view argue that it misrepresents the level at which selection primarily operates and that whole organisms — not individual genes — are the appropriate unit of analysis.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
fields.option_a: Dawkins proved that organisms, not genes, are the primary unit of natural selection.
fields.option_b: Critics agree with Dawkins that genes are the primary unit of natural selection.
fields.option_c: Dawkins proposed that evolution acts on genes rather than organisms, a view that has faced scholarly criticism.
fields.option_d: Dawkins's theory has been universally accepted in the field of evolutionary biology.
fields.explanation: The text presents Dawkins's selfish gene theory and the critics who challenge the level of selection he proposes — the main idea is the theory and its controversy.

fields.text:
Text 1: The evidence strongly suggests that reducing class sizes improves student achievement. Studies show that students in smaller classes — particularly in early grades — show consistent gains in reading and mathematics that persist into later school years.

Text 2: Class size reduction is an expensive intervention with inconsistent results across studies. Some research shows gains; other studies find minimal effects. The money spent on reducing class sizes might achieve greater impact if directed toward teacher training and quality improvement.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Text 1's claim that class size reduction 'strongly' improves achievement?
fields.option_a: Class size reduction is effective only for mathematics, not reading.
fields.option_b: The evidence is mixed, and the resources required may be better invested elsewhere.
fields.option_c: Teacher training programs are entirely ineffective compared to class size reduction.
fields.option_d: Text 1 is correct that class size reduction is the best use of educational funding.
fields.explanation: Text 2 says results are inconsistent and questions whether the money could be better spent — directly challenging Text 1's strong claim.

fields.text:
The table below shows life expectancy data across four countries:

Country A: 1950 = 52 years, 2020 = 78 years
Country B: 1950 = 46 years, 2020 = 74 years
Country C: 1950 = 61 years, 2020 = 83 years
Country D: 1950 = 44 years, 2020 = 71 years

A researcher claims that Country D showed the greatest absolute increase in life expectancy from 1950 to 2020. Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to evaluate this claim?
fields.option_a: Country D's life expectancy rose from 44 to 71, an increase of 27 years.
fields.option_b: Country D grew by 27 years, Country A by 26, Country B by 28, and Country C by 22. Country B showed the greatest increase, not Country D. The claim is incorrect.
fields.option_c: Country C had the highest life expectancy in 2020 at 83 years.
fields.option_d: All four countries showed increases in life expectancy from 1950 to 2020.
fields.explanation: D: 71−44=27; A: 78−52=26; B: 74−46=28; C: 83−61=22. Country B increased the most (28 years), so the claim about Country D is incorrect.

fields.text:
A study tracked 1,000 adults over ten years to examine the relationship between social connection and health outcomes. Participants who reported having three or more close friendships had significantly lower rates of cardiovascular disease and depression. The lead researcher concluded that social connection ________ health outcomes.

Which choice most effectively and accurately completes the claim based on what the study can actually show?
fields.option_d: is the only factor that determines
fields.explanation: An observational study can show correlation/association, not causation. 'Is associated with better' accurately reflects what the study found without overclaiming causality.

fields.text:
Text 1: Electric vehicles (EVs) are a crucial solution to climate change. They produce zero tailpipe emissions and, as electricity grids become greener, their total lifecycle emissions will continue to fall.

Text 2: The environmental benefits of EVs are often overstated. Manufacturing EV batteries requires significant energy and raw materials like lithium and cobalt, the extraction of which causes environmental harm. In regions where electricity is generated primarily from coal, EVs may not significantly reduce total emissions.

Based on the texts, both authors would likely agree that ________
fields.option_a: electric vehicles produce no emissions at any stage of their lifecycle.
fields.option_b: the environmental impact of electric vehicles depends in part on how their electricity is generated.
fields.option_c: lithium and cobalt mining has no effect on the environment.
fields.option_d: electric vehicles offer no advantages over traditional gasoline-powered cars.
fields.explanation: Text 1 acknowledges that total lifecycle emissions depend on how the grid is powered; Text 2 explicitly states this matters. Both acknowledge the grid's role.

fields.text:
The table shows the percentage of adults in four cities who commute by public transit:

City W: 2015 = 28%, 2022 = 35%
City X: 2015 = 41%, 2022 = 38%
City Y: 2015 = 19%, 2022 = 27%
City Z: 2015 = 53%, 2022 = 58%

A transit planner argues that City Y showed the largest percentage-point increase in transit commuters between 2015 and 2022. Which choice most effectively evaluates this claim using data from the table?
fields.option_a: City Y's transit ridership rose from 19% to 27%, an increase of 8 percentage points.
fields.option_b: City Y grew by 8 points (27−19), City W by 7 points (35−28), City X declined by 3 points, and City Z grew by 5 points. City Y had the largest increase. The claim is correct.
fields.option_c: City Z had the highest transit ridership in both 2015 and 2022.
fields.option_d: City X was the only city where transit ridership declined between 2015 and 2022.
fields.explanation: Y: +8, W: +7, X: −3, Z: +5. City Y had the largest increase (8 points), confirming the planner's claim.

fields.text:
The committee's final recommendations, presented after months of deliberation with stakeholders from across the region, ________ a significant departure from the policies adopted just three years earlier.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: The plural subject 'recommendations' requires the plural verb 'represent.'

fields.text:
Not only the lead researcher but also several of her graduate students ________ named as co-authors on the landmark study published in Nature.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: With 'not only A but also B,' the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Graduate students' is plural → 'were.'

fields.text:
________ extensive archival research across three countries, the historian constructed a nuanced portrait of the diplomatic negotiations leading up to the armistice.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: 'Having conducted' is the perfect participial phrase indicating the prior completed research that enabled the historian's portrait.

fields.text:
The new regulation, which applies to all manufacturers operating within the state's borders regardless of company size, ________ into effect on January 1 of next year.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: The singular subject 'regulation' requires the singular verb 'goes.'

fields.text:
The expedition team had three main objectives ________ mapping the uncharted river system, cataloguing undescribed plant species, and establishing relationships with communities in the region.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: A colon introduces the list of three objectives that elaborates on 'three main objectives.'

fields.text:
The psychologist's study was groundbreaking ________ it challenged the prevailing view that personality traits are fixed from childhood and cannot change significantly in adulthood.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses. The second clause explains why the study was groundbreaking.

fields.text:
The opera singer's performance ________ universally praised by critics — was her debut at the Metropolitan Opera, a stage she had dreamed of since childhood.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: The parenthetical 'universally praised by critics' is set off by dashes. Since the closing dash is present, the opening punctuation must also be a dash.

fields.text:
Despite the economic uncertainty of the period, the architect completed her most ambitious project in 1938 ________ a sprawling public library that remains in use today.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: A colon correctly introduces the appositive ('a sprawling public library') that identifies the ambitious project.

fields.text:
Roman concrete, known as opus caementicium, was renowned for its durability — some structures built with it have survived for over 2,000 years. ________ modern scientists were surprised to discover that Roman concrete actually becomes stronger over time as seawater penetrates it and causes minerals to crystallize within the structure.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
fields.explanation: 'Moreover' adds an additional surprising fact about Roman concrete beyond its known durability.

fields.text:
The novelist revised her manuscript seven times before submitting it to her publisher, each revision bringing her closer to the spare, precise prose she envisioned. ________ when the novel was finally published, it was praised for exactly the qualities she had worked so hard to achieve.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
fields.explanation: 'Consequently' signals that the extensive revisions led to the praised outcome — cause and effect.

fields.text:
The physicist's first paper on quantum entanglement was rejected by three major journals, each citing the unconventional nature of the claims. ________ the paper was eventually accepted and went on to become one of the most cited works in theoretical physics.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
fields.explanation: 'Ultimately' signals the final outcome after the difficulty — the paper eventually succeeded despite initial rejection.

fields.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ada Lovelace (1815–1852) is often called the world's first computer programmer.
- She worked with mathematician Charles Babbage on his Analytical Engine.
- Her notes on the Engine include an algorithm designed to compute Bernoulli numbers.
- She recognized that the Engine could be used for more than just calculation — including composing music.
- Her contributions were not widely recognized until the mid-twentieth century.

The student wants to explain why Lovelace is considered a visionary beyond her programming work. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
fields.option_a: Ada Lovelace worked with Charles Babbage on his Analytical Engine in the early nineteenth century.
fields.option_b: Lovelace wrote an algorithm to compute Bernoulli numbers, making her the world's first computer programmer.
fields.option_c: Lovelace recognized that the Analytical Engine could be used for purposes beyond calculation — such as composing music — demonstrating a visionary understanding of computing's potential.
fields.option_d: Lovelace's contributions were not widely recognized until the mid-twentieth century.
fields.explanation: Option C highlights her visionary insight that computing could go beyond calculation — the reason she is considered more than just a programmer.

fields.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The ozone layer shields Earth from harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun.
- In 1985, scientists discovered a large hole in the ozone layer above Antarctica.
- The hole was caused primarily by chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) used in refrigerants and aerosol sprays.
- The Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out CFC production in most countries.
- Scientists now project the ozone layer will recover to pre-1980 levels by 2065.

The student wants to present the Montreal Protocol as a model of successful international environmental action. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
fields.option_a: The ozone hole was discovered in 1985 above Antarctica.
fields.option_b: CFCs from refrigerants and aerosol sprays were the primary cause of ozone depletion.
fields.option_c: By phasing out CFC production through the Montreal Protocol (1987), countries took coordinated action that scientists now project will allow the ozone layer to recover to pre-1980 levels by 2065.
fields.option_d: The ozone layer protects Earth from harmful UV radiation.
fields.explanation: Option C traces the full arc: the international agreement (Montreal Protocol) led to action (phasing out CFCs) with measurable projected success (recovery by 2065) — making it the strongest case for the Protocol as a model.

fields.text: Solve for x: 5x + 8 = 33
If 2(3x − 4) = 4x + 6, what is the value of x?
Which expression is equivalent to 3(x + 2) + 2(x − 5)?
A line has equation y = −2x + 7. Which ordered pair lies on this line?
A line has equation y = −2x + 3. Which ordered pair lies on this line?

The system of equations has solution (x, y). What is x + y?
x + 2y = 10
2x − y = 5
fields.explanation: From eq2: y = 2x−5. Substitute: x + 2(2x−5) = 10 → 5x−10=10 → x=4; y=3. x+y=7.

fields.text: If g(x) = x² + 3, what is g(−3)?
A function f satisfies f(2) = 7 and f(5) = 16. If f is linear, what is f(0)?
In the xy-plane, the line y = 2x − 5 crosses the x-axis at what point?
fields.explanation: Set y = 0: 2x − 5 = 0 → x = 2.5. The x-intercept is (2.5, 0).

fields.text:
The table shows values of function h:
x: 0, 1, 2, 3
h(x): 5, 8, 11, 14

Which equation defines h(x)?
A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 17 and one leg of 8. What is the length of the other leg?
The circumference of a circle is 31.4 inches. What is its radius? (Use π ≈ 3.14)
A regular hexagon has interior angles that each measure how many degrees?
fields.explanation: Sum of interior angles of hexagon = (6−2)×180° = 720°. Each angle = 720°/6 = 120°.

fields.text: A triangle has a base of 14 cm and a height of 9 cm. What is its area?
The data set is: 8, 13, 5, 19, 10, 13, 7. What is the median?
fields.explanation: Sorted: 5, 7, 8, 10, 13, 13, 19. Median = 4th value = 10.

fields.text: A class of 24 students took a quiz. If 18 students passed, what percentage of students passed?
A standard deck of 52 cards has 4 suits of 13 cards each. If one card is drawn at random, what is the probability it is a heart?
fields.explanation: 13 hearts out of 52 cards: 13/52 = 1/4.

fields.text: The ages of seven teachers are: 28, 35, 42, 29, 55, 48, 35. What is the mode?
fields.explanation: 35 appears twice; all other values appear once. Mode = 35.

fields.text: In a survey, 45 of 180 participants chose option A. What percentage chose option A?
A recipe calls for 2.5 cups of flour to make 20 cookies. How many cups of flour are needed to make 48 cookies?
fields.explanation: Rate: 2.5/20 cups per cookie. For 48 cookies: (2.5/20) × 48 = 6 cups.

fields.text: A swimming pool holds 15,000 gallons and is currently 40% full. How many more gallons are needed to fill it completely?
Tom drove 180 miles in 3 hours, then 120 miles in 2 hours. What was his average speed for the entire trip?
fields.explanation: Total distance = 300 miles; total time = 5 hours. Average speed = 300/5 = 60 mph.

fields.text: If 5 workers can build a wall in 12 days, how many days would it take 10 workers to build the same wall?
fields.explanation: Total work = 5 × 12 = 60 worker-days. With 10 workers: 60/10 = 6 days.

fields.text: Solve for x: 3x − 5 = 10
If y = 3x + 2 and x = 4, what is y?
Which value of x satisfies 2x − 1 > 7?
fields.explanation: 2x > 8; x > 4. Among the choices, x = 5 satisfies (2(5)−1=9>7) ✓.

fields.text: What is the value of 4a − b when a = 5 and b = 3?
If x + y = 10 and x = 6, what is y?
If f(x) = 2x − 3, what is f(7)?
Which point lies on the line y = −x + 5?
Which point lies on the line y = x − 4?
The line y = 2x + 1 crosses the y-axis at which point?
fields.explanation: At x = 0: y = 2(0) + 1 = 1. The y-intercept is (0, 1).

fields.text: What is the perimeter of a rectangle with length 12 and width 5?
Two angles of a triangle measure 55° and 75°. What is the third angle?
What is the area of a square with side length 9?
fields.explanation: Area = 9² = 81.

fields.text: A right triangle has legs of 5 and 12. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
The data set is: 4, 9, 3, 7, 2. What is the median?
fields.explanation: Sorted: 2, 3, 4, 7, 9. Median = 3rd value = 4.

fields.text: A bag has 6 red balls and 4 blue balls. What is the probability of randomly selecting a red ball?
The temperatures for six days were: 68, 72, 70, 65, 74, 71. What is the mean?
There are 25 students in a class. 15 are girls. What percentage are boys?
What is the range of this data set: 14, 6, 22, 9, 18?
fields.explanation: Range = max − min = 22 − 6 = 16.

fields.text: A bicycle costs $180 and is on sale for 15% off. What is the sale price?
A school bus can hold 44 students. If 176 students need to travel, how many full buses are needed?
Ana reads 25 pages per day. How many days will it take her to read 175 pages?
A shop sells 3 pencils for $1.20. What is the cost of 12 pencils?
If 3x − 2y = 16 and x + y = 7, what is the value of y?
The sum of three consecutive integers is 81. What is the largest of the three integers?
fields.explanation: Let the integers be n, n+1, n+2. 3n+3=81 → n=26. Largest = 28.

fields.text: For what positive value of x does x² − 5x − 14 = 0?
fields.explanation: (x−7)(x+2)=0 → x=7 (positive) or x=−2.

fields.text: A clothing store marks up the wholesale price of a shirt by 40% and then offers a 25% discount on the marked-up price. If the original wholesale price is w, what is the final selling price?
fields.explanation: Marked up: 1.40w. After 25% discount: 1.40w × 0.75 = 1.05w.

fields.text: The graph of a linear equation passes through (−2, 5) and (4, −1). What is the equation of this line?
If f(x) = x² − 3x and g(x) = 2x + 1, what is f(g(2))?
The vertex of the parabola y = (x − 3)² + 4 is at which point?
fields.explanation: Vertex form y = a(x−h)² + k has vertex at (h, k) = (3, 4).

fields.text: A function f is defined by f(x) = 3x âˆ’ 7. If f(a) = 5, what is the value of a?
If f(x) = 2x + 3, for what value of x does f(x) = f(x+1)?
fields.explanation: f(x)=2x+3; f(x+1)=2(x+1)+3=2x+5. 2x+3=2x+5 gives 3=5, which is never true. No such x exists.

fields.text: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in ratio 3:5. If the area of the smaller triangle is 27 cm², what is the area of the larger triangle?
A cone has a radius of 6 and a slant height of 10. What is the lateral surface area of the cone? (Use π ≈ 3.14)
fields.explanation: Lateral SA = πrl = 3.14 × 6 × 10 = 188.4.

fields.text: In a right triangle, one acute angle measures 30°. If the hypotenuse is 20, what is the length of the side opposite the 30° angle?
fields.explanation: In a 30-60-90 triangle, the side opposite 30° = hypotenuse/2 = 20/2 = 10.

fields.text: The area of a trapezoid with parallel sides of 8 and 14 and a height of 6 is:
Nine data values have a mean of 20. When a tenth value is added, the mean becomes 21. What is the tenth value?
fields.explanation: Sum of first 9 = 180. New sum = 21×10 = 210. Tenth value = 210−180 = 30.

fields.text: Two dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum of the two dice equals 7?
A set of 8 data values has a sum of 96. Two values equal to 6 are removed. What is the new mean of the remaining values?
fields.explanation: Remaining sum = 96 − (2×6) = 84. Remaining count = 6. Mean = 84/6 = 14.

fields.text: A set of 10 numbers has a mean of 15. If 5 is added to each number in the set, what is the new mean?
fields.explanation: Adding 5 to each number increases the mean by 5: 15 + 5 = 20.

fields.text: In a class, 35% of students play a sport, 50% are in a club, and 20% do both. What percentage of students do neither?
fields.explanation: Sport or club = 35 + 50 − 20 = 65%. Neither = 100 − 65 = 35%.

fields.text: A car and a truck start from the same point and travel in opposite directions. The car travels at 55 mph and the truck at 45 mph. After how many hours will they be 250 miles apart?
fields.explanation: Combined speed = 55 + 45 = 100 mph. Time = 250/100 = 2.5 hours.

fields.text: A mixture of 40% acid solution and 70% acid solution is made to produce 60 liters of a 50% solution. How many liters of the 40% solution are needed?
A printer can print 30 pages per minute. A faster printer can print 50 pages per minute. Working together, how many minutes does it take to print 400 pages?
fields.explanation: Combined rate = 30+50 = 80 pages/min. Time = 400/80 = 5 minutes.

fields.text: Sarah invested $5,000 at 4% annual simple interest and $3,000 at 6% annual simple interest. What is her total interest earned after 2 years?

Physicist Richard Feynman was known not only for his Nobel Prize-winning research but also for his remarkable ability to ________ complex scientific concepts to general audiences without sacrificing accuracy.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Elucidate' means to explain or make clear — precisely matching the ability to clarify complex ideas for a general audience.

fields.text:
The environmental group's campaign was seen as ________ by its opponents, who argued that it exaggerated the dangers of the proposed dam and relied on misleading statistics.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Alarmist' means exaggerating dangers to cause alarm — precisely matching the opponents' criticism.

fields.text:
The ancient historian's account of the battle was long considered the definitive record, but recent archaeological discoveries have shown it to be ________ in several key respects, forcing scholars to revise the established narrative.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Inaccurate' means not correct — matching discoveries that forced scholars to revise the account.

fields.text:
Architect Zaha Hadid's flowing, curvilinear designs ________ traditional architectural conventions, replacing straight lines and right angles with sweeping forms inspired by natural landscapes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Subverted' means to undermine or challenge — matching designs that replace conventional forms.

fields.text:
Researchers studying ancient climate have used ice cores from Greenland and Antarctica to reconstruct atmospheric conditions going back hundreds of thousands of years. Tiny air bubbles trapped in the ice contain samples of ancient atmosphere, including concentrations of greenhouse gases. Analyzing these bubbles has revealed that current atmospheric CO₂ levels are higher than at any point in the past 800,000 years.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
fields.option_a: Scientists have developed ice cores specifically to measure current CO₂ levels.
fields.option_b: Ice core analysis has provided evidence that current atmospheric CO₂ is historically unprecedented.
fields.option_c: Greenland has more useful ice cores for climate research than Antarctica.
fields.option_d: Air bubbles in ice contain all the same gases as modern air.
fields.explanation: The main idea is that ice core analysis revealed current CO₂ levels are higher than at any point in the past 800,000 years.

fields.text:
The following text is adapted from Zora Neale Hurston's 1937 novel Their Eyes Were Watching God.

She was stretched on her back beneath the pear tree soaking in the alto chant of the visiting bees, the gold of the sun and the panting breath of the breeze when the inaudible voice of it all came to her. She saw a dust-bearing bee sink into the sanctum of a bloom; the thousand sister-calyxes arch to meet the love embrace and the ecstatic shiver of the tree from root to tiniest branch creaming in every blossom and frothing with delight.

Which choice best describes the overall tone of the passage?
fields.explanation: Words like 'ecstatic,' 'delight,' 'panting,' and 'frothing' create a deeply sensuous, intensely joyful tone.

fields.text:
Psychologist Carol Dweck's research on 'mindset' distinguishes between individuals with a fixed mindset — who believe intelligence is innate and unchangeable — and those with a growth mindset, who believe abilities develop through effort and learning. Studies suggest that students taught to adopt a growth mindset show significantly greater academic improvement than those not given such instruction.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
fields.option_a: Dweck's research proves that intelligence is purely innate.
fields.option_b: Students with fixed mindsets always outperform those with growth mindsets.
fields.option_c: Dweck's research shows that believing abilities can grow is associated with greater academic improvement.
fields.option_d: Mindset is determined entirely by genetics and cannot be changed.
fields.explanation: The text presents Dweck's finding that a growth mindset is associated with academic improvement.

fields.text:
Between 1960 and 1975, the number of known bird species rose dramatically as ornithologists traveled to previously unstudied regions. The rate of new species discoveries has since slowed, not because few species remain undiscovered, but because most remaining undiscovered species live in highly remote habitats that are difficult and expensive to survey. This suggests that ________

Which choice most logically completes the text?
fields.option_a: the total number of bird species on Earth has stabilized since 1975.
fields.option_b: ornithologists have little interest in discovering new bird species.
fields.option_c: logistical barriers, rather than an absence of undiscovered species, explain the slowdown.
fields.option_d: most new bird species will be found in urban rather than remote environments.
fields.explanation: The passage explicitly states that the slowdown is because remaining species are in remote habitats — logistical barriers, not absence of species.

fields.text:
Immunologist Charles Janeway proposed that the immune system recognizes invading pathogens not by detecting foreign molecules per se, but by sensing molecular patterns associated specifically with infection. His 'pattern recognition' model was initially dismissed as speculative but was later validated by the discovery of toll-like receptors — proteins that recognize exactly the kinds of patterns Janeway described.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
fields.option_a: Janeway's dismissal of earlier immunology models led to new discoveries.
fields.option_b: Janeway's initially controversial theory about immune pattern recognition was later confirmed by molecular evidence.
fields.option_c: Toll-like receptors were discovered before Janeway proposed his pattern recognition model.
fields.option_d: Janeway's model suggested that the immune system cannot distinguish between foreign and domestic molecules.
fields.explanation: The text traces the arc of Janeway's theory: initially dismissed, later validated. That arc is the main idea.

fields.text:
The table shows annual renewable energy production by source (in terawatt-hours):

Wind: 1,850 | Solar: 1,400 | Hydroelectric: 4,200 | Geothermal: 95 | Biomass: 580

A report claims that hydroelectric power accounts for more than half of all renewable energy production listed. Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to evaluate this claim?
fields.option_a: Solar (1,400) and Wind (1,850) together exceed hydroelectric production.
fields.option_b: Geothermal (95) is the smallest source of renewable energy.
fields.option_c: Total production is 8,125 TWh; hydroelectric (4,200) represents about 51.7%, confirming it accounts for more than half.
fields.option_d: Biomass (580) produces more energy than geothermal (95).
fields.explanation: Total = 8,125. Hydro = 4,200. 4,200/8,125 = 51.7% > 50%. Option C correctly calculates and evaluates the claim.

fields.text:
Text 1: The use of smartphones in classrooms should be banned. Studies show that students who use phones during class score lower on assessments and retain less material.

Text 2: Blanket bans on smartphones in classrooms are counterproductive. When integrated thoughtfully, phones can enhance learning through educational apps, research tools, and collaborative platforms.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 that phones should be banned?
fields.option_a: Text 2 would agree because the studies mentioned in Text 1 are credible.
fields.option_b: Phones can have educational value when used appropriately, so a total ban is not the right response.
fields.option_c: Text 2 acknowledges that phones hurt test scores and therefore supports a ban.
fields.option_d: Phones should only be allowed in college classrooms, not in earlier grades.
fields.explanation: Text 2's argument is that thoughtful integration — not banning — is the right approach, directly disagreeing with Text 1's call for a ban.

fields.text:
A research team tracked the number of polar bears in a specific Arctic region over four decades:

1980: 1,200 | 1990: 1,080 | 2000: 940 | 2010: 760 | 2020: 610

A scientist argues that the polar bear population declined by approximately 50% from 1980 to 2020. Which choice most effectively evaluates this claim?
fields.option_a: The population fell from 1,200 to 760 by 2010, a decline of 440 bears.
fields.option_b: The population dropped from 1,200 in 1980 to 610 in 2020, a decline of 590, or about 49% — approximately 50%. The claim is essentially correct.
fields.option_c: The largest single-decade decline occurred between 2000 and 2010.
fields.option_d: The population in 1990 was 10% lower than in 1980.
fields.explanation: 590/1200 = 49.2%, which rounds to approximately 50%. Option B correctly calculates and confirms the claim.

fields.text:
Text 1: Colonizing Mars is the logical next step for humanity. Earth's resources are finite, and establishing a second planet as a home would ensure the long-term survival of the human species.

Text 2: Mars colonization is a fantasy that distracts from urgent problems on Earth. The technology required is decades away, the costs would be astronomical, and the resources spent would be far better used to address climate change and poverty on our own planet.

Based on the texts, what do the two authors disagree about?
fields.option_a: Whether Mars has any physical resources that could support human life.
fields.option_b: Whether long-term human survival should be a priority.
fields.option_c: Whether colonizing Mars is a worthwhile use of resources given other pressing needs.
fields.option_d: Whether climate change and poverty are serious problems.
fields.explanation: Text 1 calls Mars colonization the 'logical next step'; Text 2 says the resources would be far better used for Earth's problems. The core disagreement is about resource allocation.

fields.text:
The graph shows the number of electric vehicle (EV) charging stations in four cities over two years:

City P: Year 1 = 120, Year 2 = 195 | City Q: Year 1 = 85, Year 2 = 110
City R: Year 1 = 200, Year 2 = 260 | City S: Year 1 = 45, Year 2 = 90

A city planner argues that City S showed the greatest percentage growth in EV charging stations. Which choice most effectively evaluates this claim?
fields.option_a: City S doubled its stations from 45 to 90, a 100% increase.
fields.option_b: City R had the largest absolute increase of 60 stations.
fields.option_c: City S grew by 100% (45 to 90), compared to City P at 62.5%, City Q at 29.4%, and City R at 30%. City S had the greatest percentage growth. The claim is correct.
fields.option_d: City P grew by 75 stations, more than any other city except City R.
fields.explanation: S: +100%; P: +62.5%; Q: +29.4%; R: +30%. City S had the highest percentage growth, confirming the claim.

fields.text:
The collection of ancient coins donated to the museum ________ now on display in the newly renovated east wing.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: 'Collection' is the singular subject — 'is' is the correct singular verb.

fields.text:
The students in the advanced class ________ their research projects in the school library every Tuesday afternoon for the past six weeks.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: 'Have been conducting' (present perfect continuous) correctly indicates an ongoing action that started in the past and continues to the present, consistent with 'for the past six weeks.'

fields.text:
________ through thousands of pages of declassified documents, the journalist eventually uncovered evidence of a previously unknown diplomatic agreement.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: 'Searching' is the correct participial phrase modifying the subject 'the journalist.'

fields.text:
Each of the proposals submitted by the engineering teams ________ reviewed by a panel of independent experts before a final decision is made.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: 'Will be' is the correct future passive — 'before a final decision is made' signals a future action still to occur.

fields.text:
The documentary examined three distinct but related environmental crises ________ rising sea levels, accelerating biodiversity loss, and the growing frequency of extreme weather events.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: A colon introduces the list of three crises that defines 'three distinct but related environmental crises.'

fields.text:
The scientist who developed the original theory of plate tectonics, Alfred Wegener ________ was a German meteorologist, not a geologist, which led many in the geological community to initially dismiss his ideas.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: A comma sets off the appositive 'Alfred Wegener' before the main clause. (Both sides of the appositive need commas; the sentence uses one here.)

fields.text:
The city's public transit system carried more than two million passengers last year ________ making it the busiest in the region by a significant margin.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: A comma before the participial phrase 'making it the busiest...' correctly attaches the phrase to the main clause.

fields.text:
The novel's central theme — the tension between individual freedom and social obligation ________ is explored through the experiences of three very different characters.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
fields.explanation: The parenthetical 'the tension between individual freedom and social obligation' is enclosed in dashes. Since the opening dash is present, the closing punctuation must also be a dash.

fields.text:
Scientists have known for decades that regular aerobic exercise improves cardiovascular health. ________ recent research has revealed that exercise also promotes the growth of new neurons in the hippocampus, the brain region associated with memory and learning.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
fields.explanation: 'In addition' signals that the text is adding another benefit of exercise beyond the already-known cardiovascular benefits.

fields.text:
Many early explorers relied on dead reckoning — estimating position based on known speed, direction, and time — to navigate the open ocean. ________ the method was prone to cumulative errors that could leave ships dangerously off course after long voyages.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
fields.explanation: 'However' introduces a limitation contrasting with the relied-upon method.

fields.text:
The city council unanimously approved the new park design, which features native plantings and a restored wetland habitat. ________ construction is expected to begin in the spring and be completed within eighteen months.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
fields.explanation: 'Consequently' signals that the approval led to the construction timeline — cause and effect.

fields.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Nikola Tesla (1856-1943) was an inventor and engineer who developed the AC electrical system used worldwide today.
- Tesla held over 300 patents in his lifetime.
- He designed the first hydroelectric power plant at Niagara Falls in 1895.
- Tesla and Thomas Edison were rivals who famously disagreed over AC versus DC power.
- Despite his contributions, Tesla died nearly broke and in relative obscurity.

The student wants to emphasize the contrast between Tesla's technical legacy and his personal fate. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
fields.option_a: Tesla held over 300 patents and developed AC electrical systems used worldwide.
fields.option_b: Tesla and Edison were famous rivals who disagreed over AC versus DC power.
fields.option_c: Despite developing the AC electrical system now used worldwide and holding over 300 patents, Tesla died nearly broke and largely forgotten.
fields.option_d: Tesla designed the first hydroelectric power plant at Niagara Falls in 1895.
fields.explanation: Option C juxtaposes Tesla's enormous technical legacy (AC power, 300+ patents) against his sad personal fate (broke, obscure) — directly accomplishing the contrast the student wants.

fields.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, stretching 2,300 km along the coast of Queensland, Australia.
- It is home to over 1,500 species of fish, 4,000 types of mollusk, and 240 species of birds.
- Coral bleaching events caused by rising ocean temperatures have damaged large portions of the reef.
- Since 2016, over half the coral in the northern section has died.
- The reef generates approximately $6.4 billion annually for Australia's economy.

The student wants to show the scale of damage the reef has suffered. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
fields.option_a: The Great Barrier Reef stretches 2,300 km and generates $6.4 billion annually.
fields.option_b: The reef is home to over 1,500 fish species and 240 species of birds.
fields.option_c: Since 2016, over half the coral in the northern section has died due to bleaching events caused by rising ocean temperatures.
fields.option_d: Coral bleaching events have been linked to rising ocean temperatures.
fields.explanation: Option C directly quantifies the damage (over half of northern coral dead) and names the cause — the most effective way to show the scale of harm.

fields.text:
The new community center has many programs for residents of all ages. Seniors can join exercise classes, while children can ________ painting, dancing, and other creative activities.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Attend' means to go to and participate in — the most logical action for children joining classes.

fields.text:
The marathon runner trained for months before the big race. Her dedication was ________ when she crossed the finish line in record time.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Rewarded' — her dedication paid off with a record time.

fields.text:
The farmer planted seeds in early spring and ________ tended to the crops throughout the summer, ensuring a healthy harvest in the fall.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Carefully' matches the thorough tending that leads to a healthy harvest.

fields.text:
The town was ________ by a powerful storm that uprooted trees, flooded streets, and knocked out power for thousands of residents.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
fields.explanation: 'Struck' means hit by something forceful — the most precise word for a town battered by a storm.

fields.text:
Octopuses are highly intelligent animals capable of solving puzzles, recognizing individual human faces, and using tools. Despite having no central brain region comparable to that of mammals, octopuses distribute much of their neural processing through their arms, each of which can act somewhat independently.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
fields.option_a: Octopuses are the most intelligent animals in the ocean.
fields.option_b: Octopuses lack the brain structure needed to solve puzzles or use tools.
fields.option_c: Octopuses are remarkably intelligent animals whose neural processing is uniquely distributed throughout their arms.
fields.option_d: Each arm of an octopus has a separate brain that controls the whole animal.
fields.explanation: The text establishes octopus intelligence and then explains the unusual distributed neural structure — that combination is the main idea.

fields.text:
The aurora borealis, or northern lights, appears when charged particles from the sun collide with gases in Earth's atmosphere near the poles. The different colors — greens, pinks, and reds — are caused by different types of gas at different altitudes. Green is produced by oxygen at lower altitudes, while red comes from oxygen at higher altitudes.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
fields.option_a: The aurora borealis can only be seen at the North Pole.
fields.option_b: The northern lights are caused by solar particles interacting with atmospheric gases, and different gases at different heights produce different colors.
fields.option_c: Scientists have not yet determined what causes the different colors of the aurora.
fields.option_d: The aurora borealis is the same color everywhere it appears.
fields.explanation: The text explains both the cause of the aurora and why it shows different colors — that is the main idea.

fields.text:
Florence Nightingale is remembered as a pioneer of modern nursing, but she was also a gifted statistician. During the Crimean War, she collected and analyzed data on soldier deaths and used statistical diagrams — one of the earliest uses of data visualization in public health — to convince the government to improve hospital sanitation.

Which choice best describes the function of the phrase 'one of the earliest uses of data visualization in public health' in the text?
fields.option_a: It explains why sanitation reform failed to reduce soldier deaths.
fields.option_b: It emphasizes the historical significance of Nightingale's statistical approach.
fields.option_c: It describes the specific type of data Nightingale collected.
fields.option_d: It suggests that Nightingale is primarily remembered as a statistician.
fields.explanation: The phrase highlights how historically significant Nightingale's use of statistical diagrams was — an early milestone in data visualization.

fields.text:
The Amazon tree frog survives dry seasons by coating its skin in a waxy secretion that dramatically reduces water loss. This adaptation allows it to remain active during conditions that would be fatal for most amphibians. Scientists are studying the frog's secretion for potential applications in moisturizing products and wound care.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
fields.option_a: The Amazon tree frog is the only amphibian that can survive dry conditions.
fields.option_b: Scientists have already developed commercial products from the tree frog's secretion.
fields.option_c: The Amazon tree frog has a unique biological adaptation that both aids its survival and shows promise for human applications.
fields.option_d: The Amazon tree frog's waxy coating makes it immune to all diseases.
fields.explanation: The text covers both the frog's biological adaptation for survival and its potential commercial applications — both are part of the main idea.

fields.text:
When people are asked to multitask — for example, talking on a phone while driving — their performance on both tasks typically declines. Researchers have found that the human brain does not truly perform two tasks simultaneously but rapidly switches between them. Each switch incurs a small time and accuracy cost. This suggests that ________

Which choice most logically completes the text?
fields.option_a: humans can improve multitasking ability with sufficient practice.
fields.option_b: some tasks are too simple for the brain's rapid switching to cause any performance decline.
fields.option_c: what appears to be multitasking is actually sequential processing that carries inherent performance costs.
fields.option_d: talking on a phone is always more distracting than any other secondary task.
fields.explanation: The rapid switching model, with its small costs per switch, explains why apparent multitasking results in performance decline — sequential processing with costs.

fields.text:
The table shows the results of a student survey on favorite school subjects:

Math: 32 | Science: 28 | English: 18 | History: 12 | Art: 10

A teacher states that more than half of surveyed students prefer either Math or Science. Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support this statement?
