fields.explanation: Reflecting across the y-axis replaces x with −x: y = 2(−x)+5 = −2x+5. Slope = −2.

fields.text: What is the x-intercept of the line y = 4x − 12?
fields.explanation: Set y = 0: 4x = 12 → x = 3. The x-intercept is (3, 0).

fields.text: A right triangle has one leg of 24 and hypotenuse of 26. What is the other leg?
The diameter of a circle is 18 cm. What is the area? (Use π ≈ 3.14)
In a parallelogram, two consecutive angles measure (x + 30)° and (3x − 10)°. What is x?
fields.explanation: Consecutive angles in a parallelogram are supplementary: (x+30)+(3x−10)=180 → 4x+20=180 → 4x=160 → x=40.

fields.text: A rectangular box has length 12 cm, width 8 cm, and height 5 cm. What is the surface area?
The data set is: 4, 11, 7, 14, 9, 11, 6. What is the mean?
A spinner has 8 equal sections numbered 1–8. What is the probability of spinning a number greater than 5?
fields.explanation: Numbers > 5: {6, 7, 8} — 3 out of 8. P = 3/8.

fields.text: What is the median of: 22, 35, 18, 40, 27, 31, 15?
fields.explanation: Sorted: 15, 18, 22, 27, 31, 35, 40. Median = 4th value = 27.

fields.text: A class of 32 students was surveyed. 20 have pets. What percentage do NOT have pets?
The values in a data set are 5, 8, k, 14, 18. If the mean is 11, what is k?
A student needs 85% to pass a course. She has scored 72, 90, and 88 on three tests. What must she score on the fourth test?
A student needs 84% average on 4 tests. She scored 78, 88, and 81 on the first three. What must she score on the fourth test?
A store buys shirts for $25 each and sells them for $40 each. What is the percentage markup?
Two cars leave the same city in opposite directions. Car A travels at 55 mph and Car B at 65 mph. After 3 hours, how far apart are they?
A bag of rice weighs 5 kg. 3 kg 400 g is used. How much is left?
Solve for x: x/3 + 2 = 7
If y = 3x − 4, what is y when x = 6?
What is 5m + 3n when m = 4 and n = 2?
Solve: 8x − 3 = 45
Which value satisfies 4x + 1 < 25?
fields.explanation: 4x < 24 → x < 6. Among choices, x = 5 satisfies (4(5)+1=21<25) ✓.

fields.text: If g(x) = 2x − 7, what is g(6)?
What is the slope of the line y = 5x − 9?
fields.explanation: Slope is the coefficient of x: 5.

fields.text: The line y = 3x + k passes through (2, 11). What is k?
If f(x) = x² − 9, what is f(5)?
What is the area of a circle with radius 6? (Use π ≈ 3.14)
A rectangle has perimeter 50 and length 15. What is the width?
What is the volume of a cube with side length 5 cm?
fields.explanation: V = 5³ = 125 cm³.

fields.text: In a right triangle, one acute angle is 35°. What is the other?
Find the mean of 15, 21, 9, 27, 18.
A bag has 5 yellow and 7 purple marbles. What is the probability of drawing a purple marble?
What is the mode of 3, 8, 5, 8, 11, 3, 8, 2?
fields.explanation: 8 appears 3 times — more than any other value. Mode = 8.

fields.text: What is the range of 7, 15, 4, 22, 11, 9?
If 6 items cost $18, how much do 10 items cost?
A train leaves at 9:30 AM and arrives at 1:15 PM. How long was the journey?
fields.explanation: From 9:30 to 1:15 = 3 hours 45 minutes.

fields.text: A sale reduces the price of a $90 jacket by 30%. What is the sale price?
A recipe makes 24 cookies using 3 cups of flour. How many cups are needed for 40 cookies?
fields.explanation: Rate = 3/24 = 1/8 cup per cookie. For 40: 40/8 = 5 cups.

fields.text: If (2x + 1)(x − 3) = 0 and x < 0, what is the value of 4x + 6?
If (x + 3)(x − 5) = 0 and x > 0, what is the value of 3x − 4?
For what value of k does the equation 3x + k = 2x − 7 have no solution?
fields.option_c: The equation always has a solution for any k
fields.explanation: 3x + k = 2x − 7 → x = −7 − k. This has exactly one solution for any value of k. There is no k for which it has no solution.

fields.text: What is the solution set of |2x − 4| < 6?
If 5x − 2y = 16 and 3x + y = 14, what is the value of x + y?
If 2x + 3y = 18 and 4x − y = 8, what is y?
If 3x − y = 7 and x + 2y = 14, what is x?
If f(x) = x² − 5x + 6, for what values of x does f(x) = 0?
The function f(x) = −2(x − 4)² + 9. What is the maximum value of f(x)?
fields.explanation: Maximum at vertex: f(4) = −2(0)+9 = 9.

fields.text: If f(x) = 3x + 2 and g(x) = f(x+1) − f(x), what is g(x)?
A quadratic function has zeros at x = 1 and x = 7 and opens downward. At what x-value does the maximum occur?
fields.explanation: Maximum occurs at the midpoint of the zeros: (1+7)/2 = 4.

fields.text: A sphere has surface area 100π cm². What is its radius?
fields.explanation: SA = 4πr² = 100π → r² = 25 → r = 5 cm.

fields.text: In triangle ABC, angle A = 50° and angle B = 70°. An exterior angle at C equals ________
fields.explanation: Angle C = 180−50−70 = 60°. Exterior angle = 180−60 = 120°.

fields.text: A regular octagon (8 sides) has interior angles that each measure how many degrees?
Two circles have radii in the ratio 2:5. What is the ratio of their areas?
fields.explanation: Area ratio = (2/5)² = 4/25.

fields.text: The mean of 8 numbers is 14. If two numbers with values 8 and 20 are removed, what is the mean of the remaining 6 numbers?
fields.explanation: Original sum = 112. New sum = 112−28=84. Mean = 84/6=14.

fields.text: A fair coin is flipped 3 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 2 heads?
A data set has values 10, 15, x, 25, 30. If the median is 18, what can be said about x?
fields.explanation: For the median of 5 values to be the 3rd value = 18, sorting must put 18 in the middle. If x=18: sorted = 10,15,18,25,30. Median=18 ✓.

fields.text: In a set of 5 numbers, the median is 12, the mean is 14, and the mode is 10. If the largest number is 22 and the smallest is 8, what is the sum of the remaining two numbers?
fields.explanation: Total sum = 14×5=70. Known: 8,10,12,10 (mode=10 means 10 appears at least twice),22. Wait: median=12, mode=10. If mode=10, 10 appears most. Values: 8,10,10,12,22 — sum=62≠70. Let me try: 8,10,12,10,22 fails. Need sum=70. 8+?,12,?,22. Mode=10 so 10 appears at least twice. If set is 8,10,10,12,22: sum=62. Not 70. Try 8,10,10,12,x: 5th value must be 30 to get sum=70, but then 30>22 (largest). The question has a flaw. Let me fix.

fields.text: A set of data has mean 50, median 48, and mode 45. A new value of 50 is added to the data. Which of the following must be true?
fields.option_a: The new mean is greater than 50
fields.explanation: Adding a value equal to the mean keeps the mean unchanged at 50.

fields.text: A cyclist rides 60 km at 20 km/h, then 40 km at 10 km/h. What is her average speed for the entire trip?
fields.explanation: Total distance = 100 km. Total time = 60/20 + 40/10 = 3+4 = 7 hrs. Avg = 100/7 ≈ 14.3 km/h. Closest is 14.

fields.text: A 20% salt solution is mixed with pure water to produce 80 liters of a 12% solution. How many liters of the 20% solution are used?
An item is marked up 50% from cost, then put on sale for 20% off the marked-up price. If the final price is $60, what was the original cost?
Together, Pipe X and Pipe Y fill a tank in 6 hours. Pipe X alone fills it in 10 hours. How many hours does Pipe Y alone take?

The researcher's methodology was considered ________ because it combined multiple analytical frameworks rather than relying on a single approach.

Which word most precisely completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Syncretic" means combining different systems or practices, fitting a method that merges multiple frameworks.

fields.text:
Passage: 'The ancient harbor of Alexandria was once the busiest port in the Mediterranean. Ships from across the known world docked there, carrying silk from China, spices from India, and grain from Egypt. The city's Mouseion, home to the famous Library, attracted scholars who compiled and translated texts from dozens of languages. Yet within a century of Julius Caesar's visit, much of this cosmopolitan energy had dissipated.'

What is the central claim of this passage?
fields.option_a: A) Julius Caesar was responsible for the harbor decline.
fields.option_b: B) Alexandria was a major hub of commerce and learning that later declined.
fields.option_c: C) The Library of Alexandria contained the most texts in the ancient world.
fields.option_d: D) Indian spices were the most valuable commodity in Mediterranean trade.
fields.explanation: The passage describes Alexandria as a thriving center of trade and scholarship, then notes this energy faded.

fields.text:
A study tracked reading scores of 400 students over two years. Group A (200 students) received daily silent reading time; Group B (200 students) followed a standard curriculum. At the end of the study, Group A averaged 78 out of 100, while Group B averaged 69 out of 100.

Which conclusion is best supported by the data?
fields.option_a: A) Silent reading time guarantees higher reading scores for all students.
fields.option_b: B) Students in Group A showed higher average scores than Group B.
fields.option_c: C) The standard curriculum has no educational value.
fields.option_d: D) Group B students were less intelligent than Group A students.
fields.explanation: The data shows Group A scored 9 points higher on average — a directly supported observation.

fields.text:
The committee (decided / decides) to postpone the vote until all members ________ present.

Which option correctly completes the sentence in the past tense?
fields.explanation: Since "decided" is past tense, the dependent clause should also use past tense: "were."

fields.text: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
fields.option_a: A) She loves hiking; but prefers shorter trails.
fields.option_b: B) The storm passed; the hikers resumed their trek.
fields.option_c: C) He packed; a tent, sleeping bag, and food.
fields.option_d: D) The cabin was small; cozy, and warm.
fields.explanation: A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses: "The storm passed" and "the hikers resumed their trek."

fields.text:
Sentence 1: Volcanic soil is rich in minerals. Sentence 2: Farmers in the region produce unusually fertile crops.

Which transition best connects these ideas?
fields.explanation: "Consequently" indicates that the fertile crops result from the mineral-rich volcanic soil.

fields.text: A student is writing a report on the effects of social media on teen mental health. She has found a source saying 'teens who spend more than 3 hours per day on social media report higher rates of anxiety.' Which claim is directly supported by this source?
fields.option_a: A) Social media causes anxiety in all teenagers.
fields.option_b: B) Teens using social media extensively self-report more anxiety.
fields.option_c: C) Reducing social media use will eliminate teen anxiety.
fields.option_d: D) Social media is the leading cause of teen mental health issues.
fields.explanation: The source states teens report higher anxiety — it supports the self-report finding, not causal claims about all teens.

fields.text:
The city council's decision to rezone the waterfront was met with ________ opposition from local fishermen who feared losing access to their traditional docking sites.

Which word best fills the blank?
fields.explanation: "Vociferous" means loud and forceful, fitting strong public opposition.

fields.text:
Passage: 'Mangrove forests grow along tropical coastlines, their tangled roots anchoring sediment and sheltering juvenile fish. Scientists have documented their role in buffering coastal communities from storm surges. Despite these benefits, approximately 35% of the world's mangroves have been lost since 1980, largely due to shrimp aquaculture and coastal development.'

According to the passage, why are mangrove forests ecologically valuable?
fields.option_a: A) They produce timber used in tropical construction.
fields.option_b: B) They stabilize sediment and protect coastlines while supporting fish populations.
fields.option_c: C) They reduce ocean temperatures during hurricanes.
fields.option_d: D) They provide habitat exclusively for migratory birds.
fields.explanation: The passage cites sediment anchoring, juvenile fish shelter, and storm surge buffering as the forests' ecological roles.

fields.text:
Survey data shows that 65% of teenagers prefer reading digital books, while 35% prefer print books. Among students who said they read more than 20 books per year, 70% preferred print books.

Which statement is supported by this data?
fields.option_a: A) Digital books are superior to print books for learning.
fields.option_b: B) Heavy readers are more likely to prefer print books than the general teen population.
fields.option_c: C) Most teenagers do not read books at all.
fields.option_d: D) Print books will replace digital books within a decade.
fields.explanation: Among heavy readers, 70% prefer print vs. only 35% overall — heavy readers lean toward print at a higher rate.

fields.text:
Neither the director nor the actors ________ aware that the microphones had been left on.

Which verb form is correct?
fields.explanation: With "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the nearest subject ("actors," plural), so "were" is correct.

fields.text: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
fields.option_a: A) The marathon, which is held every spring attracts thousands of participants.
fields.option_b: B) The marathon, which is held every spring, attracts thousands of participants.
fields.option_c: C) The marathon which is held every spring, attracts thousands of participants.
fields.option_d: D) The marathon which is held, every spring attracts thousands of participants.
fields.explanation: Non-restrictive clauses beginning with "which" are set off by commas on both sides.

fields.text:
Sentence 1: The new bridge design reduces material costs by 20%. Sentence 2: Engineers have expressed concern about its long-term structural integrity.

Which transition best introduces Sentence 2?
fields.explanation: "However" signals a contrasting concern following the cost benefit.

fields.text: A student is writing about the benefits of urban green spaces. He wants to include a statistic showing that parks reduce city temperatures. Which source type would be most credible for this claim?
fields.option_a: A) A blog post by a park visitor
fields.option_b: B) A peer-reviewed environmental science study
fields.option_c: C) A social media post by a city councillor
fields.option_d: D) A tourism brochure for the city
fields.explanation: Peer-reviewed scientific studies provide the most reliable empirical data for factual claims.

fields.text:
The professor's tone during the lecture was distinctly ________, making even complex philosophical debates seem simple and accessible to first-year students.

Which word best completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Lucid" means clear and easy to understand, matching the description of making complex topics accessible.

fields.text:
Passage: 'The printing press transformed medieval Europe. Before its invention, books were laboriously copied by hand, limiting literacy to clergy and wealthy nobles. Gutenberg's press allowed texts to be reproduced rapidly and cheaply, spreading knowledge across social classes. Within fifty years, millions of books circulated where previously thousands existed.'

What effect does the passage say the printing press had on literacy?
fields.option_a: A) It reduced the production of religious texts.
fields.option_b: B) It allowed knowledge to reach people beyond the clergy and nobility.
fields.option_c: C) It made Gutenberg the wealthiest man in Europe.
fields.option_d: D) It replaced Latin with vernacular languages in schools.
fields.explanation: The passage states that rapid, cheap reproduction spread knowledge across social classes — beyond clergy and nobles.

fields.text:
A school tested two homework policies over one semester. Policy A (no homework) resulted in a class average of 74%. Policy B (one hour of homework nightly) resulted in a class average of 82%. There were 30 students in each group.

What does the data most directly suggest?
fields.option_a: A) Homework is the only factor affecting student performance.
fields.option_b: B) Students with nightly homework scored higher on average than those without.
fields.option_c: C) Policy A should be eliminated in all schools.
fields.option_d: D) The difference of 8 points is too small to be meaningful.
fields.explanation: The data directly shows an 8-point average difference favoring Policy B.

fields.text:
The team of scientists ________ their findings at the international conference next month.

Which verb correctly completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Next month" signals future tense; "will present" is correct.

fields.text: Choose the sentence with correct comma usage:
fields.option_a: A) After the rain stopped the children, played outside.
fields.option_b: B) After the rain stopped, the children played outside.
fields.option_c: C) After the rain, stopped the children played outside.
fields.option_d: D) After the rain stopped the children played, outside.
fields.explanation: A comma follows an introductory adverbial clause: "After the rain stopped," before the main clause.

fields.text:
Sentence 1: The new diet reduced participants' cholesterol levels significantly. Sentence 2: Many participants found the diet difficult to maintain long-term.

Which transition most accurately connects these ideas?
fields.explanation: "Even so" concedes the benefit while introducing the contrasting challenge of sustainability.

fields.text: A researcher is studying whether music education improves math performance. She finds two studies: one showing a positive link and one showing no link. What is the most appropriate conclusion?
fields.option_a: A) Music education definitively improves math scores.
fields.option_b: B) Music education has no effect on math performance.
fields.option_c: C) The evidence is mixed; more research is needed.
fields.option_d: D) Both studies must be flawed.
fields.explanation: Conflicting studies indicate inconclusive evidence, meaning more research is needed before drawing firm conclusions.

fields.text:
Despite the apparent ________ of the task, experienced technicians completed the repair in under an hour.

Which word best completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Intricacy" means complexity or elaborateness, fitting a repair that appeared complicated but was done quickly by experts.

fields.text:
Passage: 'The monarch butterfly migration is one of nature's most spectacular phenomena. Each fall, millions of butterflies travel up to 3,000 miles from Canada to central Mexico. Scientists are still unraveling how these insects navigate with such precision over distances their individual lifespans cannot encompass — no single butterfly completes the full round trip.'

What puzzle does the passage identify about monarch migration?
fields.option_a: A) Why monarchs travel to Mexico rather than South America
fields.option_b: B) How butterflies navigate such vast distances without any individual completing the full journey
fields.option_c: C) Why the number of migrating butterflies has declined in recent years
fields.option_d: D) How monarchs survive cold temperatures during migration
fields.explanation: The passage explicitly says scientists are puzzled by how monarchs navigate precisely when no single individual completes the full round trip.

fields.text:
A graph shows that city A spent $500 per student on arts education and had a 90% graduation rate. City B spent $200 per student and had an 82% graduation rate.

Which inference is most cautious and data-supported?
fields.option_a: A) Arts spending is the direct cause of higher graduation rates.
fields.option_b: B) There is a correlation between higher arts spending and higher graduation rates in these two cities.
fields.option_c: C) All cities should immediately increase arts spending.
fields.option_d: D) City B students are less motivated academically.
fields.explanation: Correlation between two data points is supported; causation cannot be established from just two cities.

fields.text:
By the time the judges announced the winner, the contestants ________ waiting for over three hours.

Which verb form is correct?
fields.explanation: Past perfect progressive ("had been waiting") shows an action in progress before another past event.

fields.text: Which sentence correctly uses an apostrophe?
fields.option_a: A) The dog chased it's tail around the yard.
fields.option_b: B) The childrens' artwork was displayed in the hall.
fields.option_c: C) The committee presented its final report.
fields.option_d: D) The Ross' house is at the end of the street.
fields.explanation: "Its" as a possessive pronoun needs no apostrophe. The committee's report belongs to "it."

fields.text:
Sentence 1: The new app was downloaded by five million users in its first week. Sentence 2: The company struggled to handle server traffic during peak hours.

Which transition best links these sentences?
fields.explanation: The massive downloads caused the server strain — "As a result" shows that causal relationship.

fields.text:
The puppy was ________ when it saw its owner return home, wagging its tail and jumping up excitedly.

Which word best completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Ecstatic" means extremely happy and excited, matching the dog's enthusiastic behavior.

fields.text:
Passage: 'Bees are essential pollinators. As they fly from flower to flower collecting nectar, they transfer pollen, which helps plants reproduce. Without bees, many of our food crops — including apples, almonds, and berries — would not grow.'

What is the main idea of the passage?
fields.option_a: A) Bees make honey from nectar.
fields.option_b: B) Bees are critical to the reproduction of food crops through pollination.
fields.option_c: C) Apples and almonds are the most nutritious foods.
fields.option_d: D) Bees are dangerous insects that should be avoided.
fields.explanation: The passage explains how bees pollinate plants, making them essential to food crop reproduction.

fields.text:
A bar graph shows that the school library issued 200 books in January, 180 in February, and 210 in March.

Which month had the highest number of books issued?
fields.explanation: March had 210 book issues, more than January (200) and February (180).

fields.text:
The children ________ loudly in the playground when the bell rang.

Which verb form is correct?
fields.explanation: "When the bell rang" signals past tense; "played" is correct.

fields.text: Which sentence uses a period correctly?
fields.option_a: A) She finished her homework, then went to sleep.
fields.option_b: B) She finished her homework then went to sleep.
fields.option_c: C) She finished. Her homework then went to sleep.
fields.option_d: D) She finished her homework then. Went to sleep.
fields.explanation: The sentence uses a comma to separate two independent clauses joined by "then," with a correct period at the end.

fields.text:
Sentence 1: I wanted to go to the park. Sentence 2: It started raining heavily.

Which transition best connects these sentences?
fields.explanation: "However" signals that the rain contradicted the original plan to go to the park.

fields.text: A student wants to learn how a volcano erupts. Which source would be most helpful?
fields.option_a: A) A novel set near a volcano
fields.option_b: B) A science textbook chapter on volcanoes
fields.option_c: C) A travel brochure for Hawaii
fields.option_d: D) A recipe book that mentions volcano cakes
fields.explanation: A science textbook provides accurate, informative explanations of how volcanoes work.

fields.text:
The teacher was ________ with her students, always willing to explain a concept multiple times until everyone understood.

Which word best completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Patient" means calm and willing to wait or repeat, matching the teacher's described behavior.

fields.text:
Passage: 'The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert in the world, covering about 9 million square kilometers. Despite its harsh conditions, it is home to many species of animals, including fennec foxes, camels, and scorpions. Some people also live in the Sahara, in oasis communities near water sources.'

What does the passage say about life in the Sahara?
fields.option_a: A) No animals or people can survive in the Sahara.
fields.option_b: B) The Sahara is too cold for any living organisms.
fields.option_c: C) Both animals and humans live in the Sahara despite harsh conditions.
fields.option_d: D) The Sahara is shrinking due to increased rainfall.
fields.explanation: The passage mentions foxes, camels, scorpions, and human oasis communities — all living in the Sahara.

fields.text:
A pie chart shows that 50% of students prefer soccer, 30% prefer basketball, and 20% prefer tennis.

Which sport is the least popular according to the chart?
fields.explanation: Tennis has the smallest share at 20%.

fields.text:
My sister ________ her homework before dinner every evening.

Which verb form is correct for a habitual action?
fields.explanation: "Completes" (simple present) correctly expresses a habitual action.

fields.text: Which sentence correctly uses quotation marks?
fields.option_a: A) She said, "I will be there soon".
fields.option_b: B) She said "I will be there soon."
fields.option_c: C) She said, "I will be there soon."
fields.option_d: D) She said I will be there soon.
fields.explanation: A comma after "said" introduces the quotation, and the period goes inside the closing quotation marks.

fields.text:
Sentence 1: Marco studied hard all week. Sentence 2: He passed the test with a high score.

Which transition best connects these ideas?
fields.explanation: "As a result" shows that passing the test was the outcome of Marco's hard studying.

fields.text: A student is writing about the speed of cheetahs. Which source would be most reliable?
fields.option_a: A) A children's cartoon about animals
fields.option_b: B) A wildlife encyclopedia entry on cheetahs
fields.option_c: C) A friend's opinion about fast animals
fields.option_d: D) A commercial for a sports car
fields.explanation: A wildlife encyclopedia provides factual, researched information about animals.

fields.text:
The small cottage was ________, filled with comfortable furniture, warm lighting, and the smell of fresh bread.

Which word best fills the blank?
fields.explanation: "Inviting" means warm and welcoming, matching all the described cozy details.

fields.text:
Passage: 'Lightning is a discharge of electricity in the atmosphere. It forms when ice particles inside storm clouds collide, creating static electricity. When enough charge builds up, it releases as a flash of lightning. The accompanying sound — thunder — is caused by the rapid heating of air around the lightning bolt.'

According to the passage, what causes thunder?
fields.option_a: A) Ice particles colliding inside clouds
fields.option_b: B) The rapid heating of air around the lightning bolt
fields.option_c: C) Static electricity building up in storm clouds
fields.option_d: D) The flash of light from the lightning bolt
fields.explanation: The passage states that thunder is caused by the rapid heating of air around the lightning bolt.

fields.text:
A table shows average monthly temperatures in a city: June 85°F, July 92°F, August 90°F.

Which month was hottest?
fields.option_d: D) All months were the same.
fields.explanation: July at 92°F is the highest temperature of the three months.

fields.text:
Each of the students ________ required to submit a permission slip.

Which verb is correct?
fields.explanation: "Each" is singular; "was required" is correct.

fields.text: Which sentence uses a comma correctly?
fields.option_a: A) My favorite foods are pizza pasta and salad.
fields.option_b: B) My favorite foods are pizza, pasta, and salad.
fields.option_c: C) My favorite, foods are pizza pasta and salad.
fields.option_d: D) My favorite foods, are pizza pasta and salad.
fields.explanation: Commas separate items in a series: pizza, pasta, and salad.

fields.text:
Sentence 1: The museum was free to enter. Sentence 2: Many families visited on weekends.

Which transition best links these sentences?
fields.option_b: B) Because it was free to enter,
fields.explanation: "Because it was free to enter" explains why families visited — a cause-and-effect transition.

fields.text: A student is writing about how plants make food. Which source best supports this?
fields.option_b: B) A biology textbook explaining photosynthesis
fields.option_c: C) A gardening blog by a hobbyist
fields.explanation: A biology textbook provides accurate scientific information about photosynthesis.

fields.text:
The athlete was completely ________ after the marathon, barely able to walk off the course.

Which word best fits?
fields.explanation: "Exhausted" means extremely tired, matching the description of barely being able to walk after a race.

fields.text:
Passage: 'The Great Wall of China was built over many centuries by different Chinese dynasties. The most well-known sections were constructed during the Ming Dynasty (1368–1644). The wall stretches approximately 13,170 miles and was primarily built to protect China from northern invasions.'

What was the main purpose of the Great Wall?
fields.option_a: A) To serve as a trade route through China
fields.option_b: B) To mark the boundaries of the Ming Dynasty
fields.option_c: C) To protect China from northern invasions
fields.option_d: D) To impress visitors from other nations
fields.explanation: The passage explicitly states the wall was built to protect China from northern invasions.

fields.text:
A chart shows that School A has 600 students, School B has 450 students, and School C has 300 students.

How many total students attend all three schools combined?
fields.explanation: 600 + 450 + 300 = 1,350 students total.

fields.text:
Yesterday, the coach ________ the team to practice twice before the tournament.

Which verb is correct?
fields.explanation: "Yesterday" signals past tense; "asked" is correct.

fields.text: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
fields.option_a: A) Wow what an incredible performance!
fields.option_b: B) Wow, what an incredible performance!
fields.option_c: C) Wow what an incredible, performance!
fields.option_d: D) Wow, what an incredible, performance!
fields.explanation: An interjection like "Wow" is followed by a comma before the rest of the exclamatory sentence.

fields.text:
Sentence 1: The recipe called for two eggs. Sentence 2: The baker used three eggs instead.

Which transition best connects these sentences?
fields.explanation: "However" signals that the baker did something different from what the recipe stated.

fields.text: A student wants to write about the invention of the telephone. Which source provides the most reliable historical information?
fields.option_a: A) A fictional story set in the 1800s
fields.option_b: B) A history textbook chapter on communication inventions
fields.explanation: A history textbook provides accurate, well-researched historical information.

fields.text:
The senator's remarks were widely criticized as ________ — offering the appearance of compromise while actually reinforcing her original position.

Which word most precisely fits the blank?
fields.explanation: "Disingenuous" means not candid or sincere — pretending to negotiate while actually not doing so.

fields.text:
Passage: 'Epigenetics challenges the traditional view of genetics as destiny. While DNA sequence determines potential traits, epigenetic mechanisms — chemical modifications to DNA and histones — determine which genes are expressed at any given time. Strikingly, these modifications can be influenced by environmental factors such as diet, stress, and toxin exposure, and in some cases transmitted to offspring. This suggests that the boundary between nature and nurture is considerably more porous than previously thought.'

What central argument does this passage advance?
fields.option_a: A) DNA sequencing is an unreliable method of predicting traits.
fields.option_b: B) Environmental factors now replace genetic factors in determining health outcomes.
fields.option_c: C) Epigenetic research shows that environmental influences can affect gene expression and potentially heredity.
fields.option_d: D) Toxin exposure causes permanent mutations to an organism's DNA sequence.
fields.explanation: The passage argues epigenetic changes bridge nature and nurture — environmental factors affect gene expression and can be inherited.

fields.text:
A longitudinal study tracked 1,000 children from birth to age 18. Children who participated in structured extracurricular activities at age 10 were 40% more likely to graduate high school on time compared to those who did not. The study controlled for family income and school district quality.

What is the strongest conclusion the data supports?
fields.option_a: A) Extracurricular activities cause children to graduate on time.
fields.option_b: B) After controlling for key variables, early extracurricular participation correlates with higher on-time graduation rates.
fields.option_c: C) Family income is irrelevant to graduation rates.
fields.option_d: D) Children without extracurriculars are academically inferior.
fields.explanation: Even controlling for income and school quality, a strong correlation exists — though causation still cannot be definitively established.

fields.text:
Had the engineers ________ the bridge's load tolerance before construction, the collapse might have been prevented.

Which verb form is correct?
fields.explanation: In a past unreal conditional ("Had [subject]..."), the past perfect "reassessed" is correct.

fields.text: Which sentence uses a dash correctly?
fields.option_a: A) The committee — meeting on Thursday will discuss — the new policy.
fields.option_b: B) The new policy—which has been controversial since its proposal—will be reviewed Thursday.
fields.option_c: C) The new policy will be reviewed — Thursday at the committee meeting.
fields.option_d: D) The committee will meet on Thursday — and will discuss the new policy.
fields.explanation: Em dashes set off a non-essential clause in the middle of a sentence, just like commas but with more emphasis.

fields.text:
Sentence 1: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) has shown measurable success in treating anxiety disorders. Sentence 2: Access to trained CBT practitioners remains limited in rural communities.

Which transition most accurately links these ideas?
fields.option_a: A) Therefore, access to CBT should be expanded.
fields.option_b: B) Likewise, CBT is effective in treating depression.
fields.option_c: C) Despite its proven effectiveness, access to CBT practitioners remains limited in rural communities.
fields.option_d: D) For example, rural communities benefit from CBT.
fields.explanation: "Despite its proven effectiveness" acknowledges the benefit while contrasting it with the access limitation.

fields.text:
A researcher argues that intermittent fasting extends lifespan in mammals, citing three mouse studies. A critic points out that all three studies used genetically identical lab mice and that two were funded by a fasting supplement company.

What methodological concern does the critic raise?
fields.option_a: A) The studies used too few mice.
fields.option_b: B) Mouse studies can never apply to human health.
fields.option_c: C) Lack of genetic diversity and potential funding bias limit the generalizability of the findings.
fields.option_d: D) Intermittent fasting is too complex to study in a lab.
fields.explanation: The critic identifies two concerns: genetically identical subjects (limiting diversity) and funder bias (potential conflict of interest).

fields.text:
The ambassador's carefully worded statement was lauded as ________, managing to satisfy both domestic critics and foreign allies without conceding ground on any substantive issue.

Which word best fits?
fields.explanation: "Artful" means skillfully diplomatic or clever — fitting a statement that managed competing interests without concession.

fields.text:
Passage: 'Dark matter remains one of astrophysics' most vexing puzzles. Although it comprises an estimated 27% of the universe's mass-energy content, it neither emits nor absorbs light, making it invisible to conventional telescopes. Its existence is inferred entirely from its gravitational effects on visible matter — notably the anomalous rotation curves of galaxies, which rotate faster at their outer edges than Newtonian mechanics predicts without an unseen mass source.'

What is the primary evidence for dark matter's existence?
fields.option_a: A) Direct observation through infrared telescopes
fields.option_b: B) The detection of particles that absorb light in deep space
fields.option_c: C) Anomalous galaxy rotation curves that imply unseen gravitational mass
fields.option_d: D) Measurements of the universe's expansion rate
fields.explanation: The passage states that galaxy rotation anomalies — which imply unseen mass — are the key evidence for dark matter.

fields.text:
Two studies examined the effect of class size on test scores. Study 1 found that students in classes of 15 outperformed those in classes of 30 by 12 points. Study 2, using a different methodology, found no statistically significant difference between class sizes of 15 and 25.

What is the most accurate interpretation of both studies together?
fields.option_a: A) Smaller class sizes definitively improve test scores.
fields.option_b: B) Class size has no effect on test scores.
fields.option_c: C) Evidence on the relationship between class size and test scores is mixed and may depend on methodology.
fields.option_d: D) Study 2 is more reliable than Study 1.
fields.explanation: Conflicting results from two studies with different methodologies indicate a nuanced, inconclusive picture.

fields.text:
The council insisted that every proposal ________ reviewed by an independent auditor before a vote.

Which verb form is correct?
fields.explanation: After verbs of command or requirement ("insisted that"), the subjunctive mood ("be") is used.

fields.text: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
fields.option_a: A) The researchers—who had worked for three years on the project were disappointed by the results.
fields.option_b: B) The researchers, who had worked for three years on the project were disappointed by the results.
fields.option_c: C) The researchers, who had worked for three years on the project, were disappointed by the results.
fields.option_d: D) The researchers who, had worked for three years on the project, were disappointed by the results.
fields.explanation: A non-restrictive relative clause ("who had worked...") must be set off by commas on both sides.

fields.text:
Passage context: A student is arguing that arts education improves critical thinking. She includes evidence that students in arts programs score higher on analytical reasoning tests.

Which transition would best introduce a counterargument?
fields.option_a: A) Furthermore, arts programs face funding cuts in many districts.
fields.option_b: B) Critics argue, however, that correlation between arts enrollment and reasoning scores may reflect pre-existing differences in student motivation.
fields.option_c: C) In addition, visual arts specifically improve spatial reasoning.
fields.option_d: D) Therefore, all schools should double their arts program funding.
fields.explanation: The counterargument introduces an alternative explanation (student motivation) that challenges the causal interpretation of the correlation.

fields.text: A student is writing a paper arguing that social media platforms should be regulated like public utilities. She wants to include evidence that is both empirical and directly relevant to policy. Which source would be most appropriate?
fields.option_a: A) A personal essay by a teenager about social media addiction
fields.option_b: B) A philosophy journal article on the ethics of free speech
fields.option_c: C) A peer-reviewed economics paper measuring market concentration in social media platforms
fields.option_d: D) A news editorial calling for stricter internet regulations
fields.explanation: Empirical economic data on market concentration directly supports a policy argument about utility-style regulation.

fields.text:
The novel's protagonist was ________ in her convictions, refusing to alter her testimony despite intense social pressure and the threat of professional consequences.

Which word best fits?
fields.explanation: "Resolute" means admirably determined and unwavering, matching the protagonist's steadfast refusal to change her testimony.

fields.text:
Passage: 'John Maynard Keynes argued that during economic recessions, private sector demand collapses and government must step in as the spender of last resort. His critics — particularly the Austrian school — contended that government intervention distorts market signals and prolongs recoveries by preventing the correction of prior malinvestments. The debate between these schools has shaped fiscal policy debates for nearly a century.'

According to the passage, what do Austrian economists argue about government intervention in recessions?
fields.option_a: A) It is a necessary tool for stabilizing demand.
fields.option_b: B) It should be targeted exclusively at infrastructure projects.
fields.option_c: C) It distorts markets and may delay economic recovery.
fields.option_d: D) It works best when combined with monetary policy.
fields.explanation: The passage states Austrian economists believe government intervention distorts market signals and prolongs recoveries.

fields.text:
A meta-analysis reviewed 50 studies on the effect of sleep duration on cognitive performance. Studies with sample sizes over 500 consistently found a significant positive effect; studies with smaller samples showed mixed results.

What is the most methodologically sound interpretation?
fields.option_a: A) Sleep duration has no meaningful effect on cognition.
fields.option_b: B) Small studies are always unreliable.
fields.option_c: C) Larger, more statistically powered studies suggest sleep duration positively affects cognition; smaller studies are less definitive.
fields.option_d: D) All 50 studies reached the same conclusion about sleep.
fields.explanation: Larger samples provide greater statistical power; the pattern in large studies is the strongest evidence, while small studies' mixed results reflect lower power.

fields.text:
If the experiment ________ conducted under controlled conditions, the results would have been more reliable.

Which verb form is correct?
fields.explanation: This is a past counterfactual: "If it had been conducted..." uses past perfect in the conditional clause.

fields.text: Identify the correctly punctuated sentence:
fields.option_a: A) The study, published in 2023 showed that exercise, when done consistently improves mood.
fields.option_b: B) The study published in 2023, showed that exercise when done consistently, improves mood.
fields.option_c: C) The study, published in 2023, showed that exercise, when done consistently, improves mood.
fields.option_d: D) The study published in 2023 showed that exercise when done consistently improves mood.
fields.explanation: Both parenthetical phrases ("published in 2023" and "when done consistently") require commas on both sides.

fields.text:
A paragraph argues that electric vehicles (EVs) will dominate the market by 2040. The next sentence introduces data showing that EV adoption is slower in rural areas due to charging infrastructure gaps.

Which transition best introduces this limiting evidence?
fields.option_a: A) Furthermore, rural adoption rates are critical.
fields.option_b: B) This projection, however, may underestimate infrastructure barriers in rural regions.
fields.option_c: C) Therefore, EV adoption will be universal by 2040.
fields.option_d: D) Similarly, rural areas face transportation challenges.
fields.explanation: "This projection, however..." concedes the optimistic forecast while introducing a qualifying limitation.

fields.text: A scientist claims that a new drug reduces symptoms of insomnia. The only supporting evidence is a single randomized controlled trial with 50 participants over two weeks. What is the most significant limitation of this evidence?
fields.option_a: A) Randomized controlled trials are not valid research designs.
fields.option_b: B) The study is too short and too small to support broad claims about the drug's effectiveness.
fields.option_c: C) Insomnia cannot be studied in a clinical setting.
fields.option_d: D) The drug should be tested on animals before humans.
fields.explanation: A small sample (50) and short duration (two weeks) limit the generalizability and reliability of the findings.

fields.text:
The philanthropist's decision to donate anonymously was seen as an act of genuine ________, unsullied by any desire for public recognition.

Which word best completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Altruism" means selfless concern for others — perfectly matching anonymous giving without seeking recognition.

fields.text:
Passage: 'The concept of "nudge theory," popularized by Thaler and Sunstein, proposes that small, non-coercive changes to the environment in which choices are made can significantly influence behavior. A classic example is placing healthier foods at eye level in a cafeteria — not forbidding unhealthy choices, but making the better option easier to notice and select. Critics argue that nudges can be manipulative precisely because they operate below the level of conscious deliberation.'

What is the critics' objection to nudge theory?
fields.option_a: A) Nudges are too expensive to implement at scale.
fields.option_b: B) Nudges violate laws against government regulation of personal choices.
fields.option_c: C) Nudges may manipulate behavior without engaging people's conscious reasoning.
fields.option_d: D) Nudge theory has not been tested in real-world settings.
fields.explanation: The critics' concern is that nudges bypass conscious deliberation — shaping behavior in ways people are unaware of.

fields.text:
A researcher comparing two teaching methods collected pre-test and post-test scores from two classes. Class A (traditional instruction) improved by an average of 8 points. Class B (project-based learning) improved by an average of 14 points. However, Class B started with significantly lower pre-test scores.

What is the most important caveat when interpreting these results?
fields.option_a: A) Class A's improvement was negligible.
fields.option_b: B) Pre-test score differences mean Class B had more room to improve, making the comparison less straightforward.
fields.option_c: C) Project-based learning is definitively superior to traditional instruction.
fields.option_d: D) The researcher should have used a different scoring rubric.
fields.explanation: Regression to the mean and ceiling effects mean a class starting lower has more room to improve — making raw gain scores incomparable.

fields.text:
The legislation requires that every contractor ________ proof of insurance before beginning work on public property.

Which verb form is correct?
fields.explanation: The subjunctive mood follows "requires that": "provide" (not "provides") is correct.

fields.text: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
fields.option_a: A) The attorney argued that the evidence was inadmissible; the judge however, disagreed.
fields.option_b: B) The attorney argued that the evidence was inadmissible; the judge, however, disagreed.
fields.option_c: C) The attorney argued that the evidence was inadmissible, the judge however disagreed.
fields.option_d: D) The attorney argued that the evidence was inadmissible the judge; however, disagreed.
fields.explanation: "However" used as a conjunctive adverb must be set off by a comma. The semicolon before it correctly joins the two independent clauses.

fields.text:
A student's essay claims that urban farming can significantly reduce food deserts. The next sentence will acknowledge a limitation of urban farming.

Which sentence best introduces the limitation using an appropriate transition?
fields.option_a: A) Urban farming has many benefits.
fields.option_b: B) Admittedly, urban farming faces scalability challenges that may limit its impact in the largest and most underserved food deserts.
fields.option_c: C) Therefore, urban farms should be built in all cities immediately.
fields.option_d: D) Similarly, community gardens can supplement food access.
fields.explanation: "Admittedly" is a concessive transition that introduces a limitation while maintaining the argument's overall credibility.

fields.text: If 4x − 7 = 2x + 9, what is the value of x?
A function f(x) = 3x − 4. What is f(5)?
A triangle has angles measuring 40°, 75°, and x°. What is the value of x?
fields.explanation: Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°. x = 180 − 40 − 75 = 65.

fields.text: In a dataset of 7 values: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, what is the median?
fields.explanation: The median of 7 ordered values is the 4th value: 9.

fields.text: A bookstore sold 120 books in the morning and 95 books in the afternoon. If each book costs $12, what was the total revenue for the day?
Solve for y: 3(y + 4) = 2y + 19
Which equation represents a line with slope −2 and y-intercept 5?
fields.explanation: Slope-intercept form y = mx + b: slope = −2, y-intercept = 5 → y = −2x + 5.

fields.text: A rectangle has a length of 14 cm and a width of 9 cm. What is its area?
fields.explanation: Area = length × width = 14 × 9 = 126 cm².

fields.text: A bag contains 5 red, 3 blue, and 2 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the probability of drawing a blue marble?
A train travels 270 km in 3 hours. At the same speed, how long will it take to travel 450 km?
fields.explanation: Speed = 270/3 = 90 km/h. Time = 450/90 = 5 hours.

fields.text: If 5a + 3 = 28, what is the value of 2a?
The graph of y = x² − 4 crosses the x-axis at which x-values?
A circle has a diameter of 10 cm. What is its circumference? (Use π ≈ 3.14)
A student scored 72, 85, 90, 78, and 95 on five tests. What is the mean score?
A shirt originally costs $45. It is on sale for 20% off. What is the sale price?
What is the solution to the inequality 3x − 5 > 10?
If f(x) = x² + 2x − 3, what is f(−1)?
Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. If one interior angle is 65°, what is the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle?
fields.explanation: Co-interior angles are supplementary: 180° − 65° = 115°.

fields.text: In a class of 30 students, 18 play soccer and 12 play basketball. If 6 play both, how many play neither?
fields.explanation: By inclusion-exclusion: 18 + 12 − 6 = 24 play at least one sport. 30 − 24 = 6 play neither.

fields.text: Carlos earns $14 per hour and works 35 hours per week. He spends 30% of his earnings on rent. How much does he spend on rent per week?
fields.explanation: Weekly earnings = 14 × 35 = $490. Rent = 0.30 × 490 = $147.

fields.text: The sum of three consecutive integers is 78. What is the largest integer?
fields.explanation: Let integers be n, n+1, n+2. 3n + 3 = 78 → 3n = 75 → n = 25. Largest = 27.

fields.text: A linear function passes through (0, 3) and (4, 11). What is the slope?
What is the value of 8x when x = 3?
If f(x) = 4x + 1, what is f(2)?
A square has sides of length 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
fields.explanation: Perimeter = 4 × 6 = 24 cm.

fields.text: A spinner has 4 equal sections numbered 1 through 4. What is the probability of landing on 3?
fields.explanation: P(3) = 1/4, since there are 4 equally likely outcomes.

fields.text: A box contains 24 crayons. If 8 crayons are given away, how many remain?
fields.explanation: 24 − 8 = 16 crayons remain.

fields.text: Solve for x: x + 11 = 20
Which point lies on the line y = 2x + 1?
fields.explanation: y = 2(2) + 1 = 5. The point (2, 5) lies on the line.

fields.text: A rectangle has a length of 8 m and a width of 5 m. What is its perimeter?
In a class of 20 students, 5 received A grades. What percentage of the class received an A?
A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. If 3 slices are eaten, what fraction of the pizza remains?
fields.explanation: 8 − 3 = 5 slices remain. Fraction = 5/8.

fields.text: If 2y = 18, what is the value of y + 5?
A line has slope 3 and passes through the origin. Which equation represents this line?
fields.explanation: Through the origin (b = 0) with slope 3: y = 3x.

fields.text: An equilateral triangle has sides of 9 cm. What is its perimeter?
fields.explanation: Perimeter = 3 × 9 = 27 cm.

fields.text: The ages of five children are 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11. What is the range?
A car travels at 60 km/h. How far does it travel in 2.5 hours?
fields.explanation: Distance = speed × time = 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

fields.text: What is the value of 5(3 + 4) − 10?
What is the y-intercept of the line y = −3x + 7?
fields.explanation: The y-intercept is the constant term when x = 0: b = 7.

fields.text: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
fields.explanation: Area = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².

fields.text: From a group of 10 students, 2 will be randomly selected to give a speech. What is the probability the first student chosen is named Maria (1 out of 10 students)?
fields.explanation: P(Maria is first) = 1/10.

fields.text: A store sells apples for $0.50 each. How much do 14 apples cost?
Solve: 6 − 2x = 14
If the graph of y = f(x) passes through (0, 5) and (1, 7), what is the slope of the line?

A system of equations:
2x + 5y = 24
4x âˆ’ y = 4

What is the value of x + y?
fields.explanation: Multiply eq2 by 5: 20x-5y=20. Add to eq1: 22x=44 -> x=2. y=4(2)-4=4. x+y=6.

fields.text: The function f(x) = ax² + bx + c has roots at x = −3 and x = 5, and a leading coefficient of 1. What is the value of f(0)?
A right triangle has legs of 8 cm and 15 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
A data set has a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 5. A new value of 65 is added. Compared to the other values, this new value is:
fields.option_a: A) Within 1 standard deviation of the mean
fields.option_b: B) Between 1 and 2 standard deviations from the mean
fields.option_c: C) Exactly 2 standard deviations from the mean
fields.option_d: D) More than 2 standard deviations from the mean
fields.explanation: |65 − 50| / 5 = 15/5 = 3 standard deviations above the mean — more than 2.

fields.text: Two pipes fill a tank. Pipe A fills it in 6 hours, Pipe B fills it in 4 hours. If both work together, how long does it take to fill the tank?
If x² − 9x + 20 = 0, what are the solutions?
fields.explanation: Factor: (x − 4)(x − 5) = 0 → x = 4 or x = 5.

fields.text: A quadratic function has vertex at (3, −4) and leading coefficient 2. Which equation represents this function?
fields.explanation: Vertex form: f(x) = a(x − h)² + k = 2(x − 3)² − 4, with vertex (h, k) = (3, −4).

fields.text: A cylinder has radius 5 cm and height 12 cm. What is its volume? (Use π ≈ 3.14)

In a sample of 200 voters, 120 support Candidate A and 80 support Candidate B. If a 95% confidence interval for the true proportion supporting A has a margin of error of ±7%, which interval is correct?
fields.explanation: Sample proportion = 120/200 = 60%. Interval = 60% ± 7% = (53%, 67%).

fields.text: A company's profit P (in thousands of dollars) is modeled by P = −2t² + 16t − 24, where t is years since launch. In which year(s) does the company break even (P = 0)?
The equation 2x² + 8x + 6 = 0 has roots r and s. What is the value of r × s?
fields.explanation: By Vieta's formulas for ax² + bx + c = 0: product of roots = c/a = 6/2 = 3.

fields.text: A function f is defined as f(x) = |2x − 6|. For which value(s) of x does f(x) = 4?
Two similar triangles have perimeters 24 cm and 36 cm. If the area of the smaller triangle is 48 cm², what is the area of the larger triangle?
fields.explanation: Scale factor of sides = 36/24 = 3/2. Area ratio = (3/2)² = 9/4. Area of larger = 48 × 9/4 = 108 cm².

fields.text: A box contains 4 red, 5 blue, and 6 green balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability both are red?
An investment of $5,000 grows at 6% annual compound interest. What is the value after 2 years?
If f(x) = x² − 4 and g(x) = 2x − 1, for what values of x does f(x) = g(x)?
If g(x) = 2f(x − 1) + 3 and f(x) = x², what is g(3)?
A regular hexagon has a side length of 6 cm. What is its area? (Area of regular hexagon = (3√3/2)s²)
A linear regression of study hours (x) vs. test scores (y) gives y = 5x + 60. A student studies for 7 hours. What test score does the model predict?
A car depreciates in value by 15% each year. If it is worth $20,000 now, what will it be worth after 3 years?
The product of two consecutive even integers is 168. What are the integers?
A function f(x) = 3^x. For which value of x does f(x) = 27?

A paleontologist studying fossilized remains noted that the specimen's bone structure was ________, displaying characteristics common to both reptiles and early mammals, making classification difficult.

Which word most precisely completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Mosaic" means composed of diverse elements, fitting a specimen showing traits of two distinct groups.

fields.text:
The following text is from a 2023 marine biology report.

Researchers studying bioluminescent organisms in the deep ocean found that certain jellyfish produce light not for communication, as previously assumed, but as a ________ mechanism — blinding predators long enough to escape.

Which word most logically completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: The context describes blinding predators to escape, which is a defensive function.

fields.text:
The city council's new zoning policy was described by critics as ________ because it appeared to resolve the housing shortage on paper while doing little to address the root causes of displacement.

Which word best completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Superficial" means addressing surface appearance without depth, matching the critique described.

fields.text:
The following text is adapted from a 1902 essay on industrial reform.

The factory conditions that laborers endured were not merely uncomfortable — they were ________, stripping workers of dignity, safety, and any reasonable expectation of fair treatment.

As used in the text, which word best fills the blank?
fields.explanation: "Degrading" means humiliating and stripping dignity, consistent with the extreme negative description.

fields.text:
Passage: 'The monarch butterfly's migration from Canada to central Mexico spans over 3,000 miles and involves millions of individuals. Remarkably, no single butterfly completes the full round trip — it takes three to four generations to return. Scientists believe the butterflies navigate using a time-compensated sun compass, adjusting their flight direction based on the position of the sun relative to the time of day.'

What is the main purpose of this passage?
fields.option_a: A) To argue that monarch butterflies are endangered.
fields.option_b: B) To describe the remarkable navigation and generational nature of monarch migration.
fields.option_c: C) To compare butterfly migration to bird migration.
fields.option_d: D) To explain why butterflies cannot survive Canadian winters.
fields.explanation: The passage describes how the migration works across generations and how butterflies navigate — its main focus.

fields.text:
Passage: 'For centuries, historians assumed that the Bronze Age Collapse around 1200 BCE was caused by a single catastrophic event — perhaps an invasion by the so-called Sea Peoples. Modern scholarship, however, favors a systems collapse model: droughts, earthquakes, trade disruptions, and internal rebellions combined to overwhelm the interconnected palace economies of the eastern Mediterranean simultaneously.'

Which statement best reflects the shift described in the passage?
fields.option_a: A) Historians now believe the Sea Peoples were not a real group.
fields.option_b: B) The Bronze Age Collapse is better explained by multiple converging factors than by a single cause.
fields.option_c: C) Earthquakes were the primary cause of the Bronze Age Collapse.
fields.option_d: D) Trade disruptions had no role in the collapse of Bronze Age civilizations.
fields.explanation: The passage contrasts the old single-cause theory with the modern multi-factor systems collapse model.

fields.text:
Passage: 'In the early 20th century, American women entered the workforce in large numbers during World War I, taking on roles in factories, transportation, and government offices previously held by men. When soldiers returned after the war, many women were displaced from these positions. Yet the experience had fundamentally altered expectations: women had demonstrated their capability in a wide range of occupations, and the suffrage movement gained significant momentum in the years that followed.'

According to the passage, what was one long-term effect of women entering the workforce during World War I?
fields.option_a: A) Women permanently kept all jobs previously held by men.
fields.option_b: B) The government created laws preventing women from working after the war.
fields.option_c: C) Women's proven capabilities contributed to the growing suffrage movement.
fields.option_d: D) Factories became exclusively staffed by women during the 1920s.
fields.explanation: The passage states that women's demonstrated capabilities helped fuel the suffrage movement.

fields.text:
The following text is adapted from a 2021 environmental science article.

Urban heat islands — city areas significantly warmer than surrounding rural regions — form when natural land cover is replaced by pavement and buildings that absorb and re-emit heat. Studies show that low-income neighborhoods in major U.S. cities experience higher heat island effects on average, partly because they have fewer trees and green spaces. Some cities have begun tree-planting initiatives to address this disparity.

What problem are some cities attempting to address through tree-planting initiatives?
fields.option_a: A) The overall warming of the planet due to greenhouse gases.
fields.option_b: B) The unequal distribution of heat island effects across income levels.
fields.option_c: C) The shortage of lumber in urban construction projects.
fields.option_d: D) Air pollution from automobile traffic in city centers.
fields.explanation: The passage links fewer trees in low-income areas to greater heat island effects, which is the disparity tree planting aims to fix.

fields.text:
A survey of 500 high school students asked how many hours per week they spent on extracurricular activities. The average for students with a GPA above 3.5 was 6.2 hours per week, while the average for students with a GPA below 3.0 was 3.1 hours per week.

Which conclusion is best supported by this data?
fields.option_a: A) Participating in extracurriculars causes students to earn higher grades.
fields.option_b: B) Students with higher GPAs spent more time on extracurriculars on average.
fields.option_c: C) Students with low GPAs do not participate in any extracurricular activities.
fields.option_d: D) Extracurricular activities should be required for all students.
fields.explanation: The data shows a correlation in hours, not causation. Only the factual comparison (B) is directly supported.

fields.text:
Researchers studying plant growth conducted an experiment with three groups of identical seedlings. Group 1 received 8 hours of light daily; Group 2 received 12 hours; Group 3 received 16 hours. After 30 days, average plant heights were 14 cm, 21 cm, and 19 cm respectively.

What does the data most clearly suggest?
fields.option_a: A) Plants always grow taller with more light exposure.
fields.option_b: B) 12 hours of light produced the tallest average growth in this experiment.
fields.option_c: C) Group 3 plants were defective and should be excluded from the results.
fields.option_d: D) Light has no measurable effect on plant growth.
fields.explanation: The data shows Group 2 (12 hrs) had the tallest average at 21 cm — directly supported by the numbers.

fields.text:
A city tracked the number of traffic accidents at a particular intersection before and after installing a roundabout. In the two years before installation, there were 47 accidents. In the two years after, there were 11 accidents.

A researcher claims the roundabout significantly improved safety at the intersection. Which statement best evaluates this claim?
fields.option_a: A) The claim is unsupported because two years is not long enough to draw conclusions.
fields.option_b: B) The claim is well-supported because accidents dropped by more than 75%.
fields.option_c: C) The claim is unsupported because roundabouts are known to cause more accidents.
fields.option_d: D) The claim is well-supported because no accidents occurred after installation.
fields.explanation: The drop from 47 to 11 accidents is a 77% reduction, which strongly supports the safety improvement claim.

fields.text:
Each of the scientists on the research team ________ responsible for submitting a weekly progress report to the project director.

Which verb form correctly completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Each" is a singular subject and requires the singular verb "is."

fields.text:
The documentary film crew, along with its producers and editors, ________ expected to arrive at the filming location by sunrise.

Which verb correctly completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: The core subject is "crew" (singular). Phrases beginning with "along with" do not change the subject's number.

fields.text:
By the time the rescue team reached the stranded hikers, the storm ________ for six hours.

Which verb form best completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: Past perfect progressive ("had been raging") is correct for an action continuing up to a past moment.

fields.text:
Neither the principal nor the teachers ________ aware of the planned assembly until the morning of the event.

Which verb correctly completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: With "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the nearest subject — "teachers" (plural), so "were."

fields.text: Which sentence correctly uses a colon?
fields.option_a: A) She had three goals: to graduate, to travel, and to write a novel.
fields.option_b: B) She had three goals: that included graduating, traveling, and writing.
fields.option_c: C) She had: three goals to accomplish before turning thirty.
fields.option_d: D) She: wanted to graduate, travel, and write a novel.
fields.explanation: A colon correctly introduces a list after a complete independent clause.

fields.text: Which sentence correctly uses an apostrophe?
fields.option_a: A) The childrens' artwork was displayed in the hallway.
fields.option_b: B) The childrens artwork was displayed in the hallway.
fields.option_c: C) The children's artwork was displayed in the hallway.
fields.option_d: D) The childrens's artwork was displayed in the hallway.
fields.explanation: "Children" is an irregular plural; the possessive is formed by adding 's: "children's."

fields.text: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
fields.option_a: A) The old, weathered, barn stood at the edge of the property.
fields.option_b: B) The old weathered barn stood at the edge of the property.
fields.option_c: C) The old, weathered barn stood at the edge of the property.
fields.option_d: D) The, old weathered, barn stood at the edge of the property.
fields.explanation: "Old" and "weathered" are coordinate adjectives and should be separated by a comma. No comma between "weathered" and "barn."

fields.text:
Sentence 1: The new medication showed promising results in clinical trials. Sentence 2: Regulators have not yet approved it for public use.

Which transition word best connects these two sentences?
fields.explanation: "However" signals a contrast between the promising trial results and the lack of regulatory approval.

fields.text:
Sentence 1: Plastic pollution has reached remote Arctic regions. Sentence 2: Microplastics have been found in the tissues of deep-sea fish.

Which transition best introduces Sentence 2?
fields.explanation: "Moreover" adds another example of the widespread nature of plastic pollution, extending the first point.

fields.text:
The early settlement relied entirely on trade with neighboring villages. ________, once the railroad arrived, the town grew rapidly into a self-sufficient commercial hub.

Which transition fits the shift in the passage?
fields.explanation: "Subsequently" signals a chronological sequence — after the railroad, the town changed.

fields.text:
A student is writing a report on the health effects of screen time in adolescents. She finds the following sources:
1. A 2022 peer-reviewed study linking more than 4 hours of daily screen time to increased anxiety in teens.
2. A blog post by a tech company claiming screens have no proven negative effects.
3. A 2019 meta-analysis of 30 studies finding mixed results on screen time and mental health.

Which source would most strengthen the claim that screen time harms adolescent mental health?
fields.explanation: The peer-reviewed study (1) and the meta-analysis (3) together provide the strongest evidence, though Source 3 shows mixed results and Source 1 directly supports the claim.

fields.text: A researcher wants to support the claim: "Urban green spaces reduce stress in city residents." Which of the following pieces of evidence would best support this claim?
fields.option_a: A) A survey showing that city residents prefer parks over shopping malls.
fields.option_b: B) A controlled study measuring cortisol levels in residents before and after visiting a park, showing a significant decrease.
fields.option_c: C) An article describing the history of public parks in New York City.
fields.option_d: D) A report on the cost of maintaining urban parks.
fields.explanation: Measured cortisol levels (a stress hormone) before and after park visits directly supports the stress-reduction claim with biological evidence.

fields.text: A student argues: "Students who eat breakfast perform better on standardized tests." Which evidence would WEAKEN this argument?
fields.option_a: A) A study showing a 12% score improvement in breakfast-eating students.
fields.option_b: B) A finding that students who eat breakfast also tend to sleep more hours per night.
fields.option_c: C) Data showing breakfast programs increased participation in 80% of schools.
fields.option_d: D) A report that schools with breakfast programs have higher attendance.
fields.explanation: If breakfast-eaters also sleep more, sleep (not breakfast) might explain the performance improvement, weakening the causal claim.

fields.text:
The following text is adapted from a 2020 economics article.

The startup's rapid growth was seen as ________ by industry analysts — a clear signal that the market was ready for a new approach to digital payments.

Which word most precisely completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Indicative" means serving as a sign or signal, which fits "a clear signal that the market was ready."

fields.text:
The following text is adapted from a 2022 article on ocean currents.

The thermohaline circulation — often called the ocean conveyor belt — moves water around the globe based on differences in temperature and salinity. Cold, salty water is denser and sinks near the poles, while warmer, fresher water rises near the equator. This circulation distributes heat across the planet and is a key driver of regional climates. Scientists warn that melting polar ice could disrupt this system by introducing large volumes of fresh water.

What concern do scientists raise in the passage?
fields.option_a: A) Ocean currents are moving faster than expected due to global warming.
fields.option_b: B) The thermohaline circulation may be disrupted by freshwater from melting ice.
fields.option_c: C) Warmer water is sinking near the equator, reversing the conveyor belt.
fields.option_d: D) Regional climates are becoming more uniform as the ocean conveyor belt speeds up.
fields.explanation: The passage explicitly states scientists warn that melting ice could disrupt thermohaline circulation by adding fresh water.

fields.text:
The following text is from a short story set in a small fishing village.

'The harbor was still before dawn, the water flat as hammered tin. Old Cerro had launched his dinghy every morning for forty years from this same dock. He did not think of this as routine — he thought of it as something close to prayer. The creak of the oarlocks, the smell of brine, the way the horizon swallowed the last of the stars. These were his liturgy.'

What does the author most likely mean by calling Cerro's morning routine a 'liturgy'?
fields.option_a: A) Cerro is a deeply religious man who prays on the water.
fields.option_b: B) The fishing routine has a ritualistic, almost sacred quality for Cerro.
fields.option_c: C) Cerro resents having to fish every morning and wishes for a change.
fields.option_d: D) The harbor is used as a place of worship by the village community.
fields.explanation: Using words like "prayer" and "liturgy" (a religious ritual) conveys that the routine holds deep, almost sacred meaning for Cerro.

fields.text:
The puppy was ________ excited about the walk that it ran in circles before the leash was even attached.

Which word best completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "So...that" is a standard construction showing degree: "so excited that it ran in circles."

fields.text:
The weather forecast predicted rain, but the morning turned out to be bright and ________.

Which word best completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Sunny" contrasts with the predicted rain and fits the description of a bright morning.

fields.text:
The librarian asked the students to speak in ________ voices so they wouldn't disturb others who were reading.

Which word best completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: A library setting and the reason given (not disturbing others) calls for "quiet" voices.

fields.text:
The old bicycle was too ________ to ride safely — both tires were flat and the brakes barely worked.

Which word best completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: Flat tires and broken brakes make the bicycle "dangerous" to ride.

fields.text:
Passage: 'Penguins are birds that cannot fly, but they are excellent swimmers. Their wings have evolved into flippers, which help them move quickly through the water to catch fish. Penguins live mostly in the Southern Hemisphere, especially in Antarctica.'

According to the passage, why are penguins good swimmers?
fields.option_a: A) They have hollow bones that make them float.
fields.option_b: B) Their wings have evolved into flippers suited for swimming.
fields.option_c: C) They have waterproof scales like fish.
fields.option_d: D) They practice swimming from birth.
fields.explanation: The passage directly states that penguin wings evolved into flippers that help them swim.

fields.text:
Passage: 'The rainforest receives over 80 inches of rain per year. This constant moisture supports an enormous variety of plant and animal life. Scientists estimate that more than half of all species on Earth live in tropical rainforests, even though these forests cover only about 6% of the planet's surface.'

Which statement is directly supported by the passage?
fields.option_a: A) Rainforests will disappear within 50 years.
fields.option_b: B) Tropical rainforests cover more than half the planet.
fields.option_c: C) More than half of Earth's species live in tropical rainforests.
fields.option_d: D) Rainfall is the only factor that supports rainforest biodiversity.
fields.explanation: The passage explicitly states that scientists estimate more than half of all species live in tropical rainforests.

fields.text:
Passage: 'The Eiffel Tower was built in 1889 as the entrance arch for the 1889 World's Fair in Paris. It was designed by engineer Gustave Eiffel. At the time, many Parisians disliked the tower, calling it ugly. Today, it is one of the most visited monuments in the world, attracting about 7 million visitors each year.'

How did Parisians initially react to the Eiffel Tower?
fields.option_a: A) They celebrated it as a masterpiece of engineering.
fields.option_b: B) They found it too expensive to maintain.
fields.option_c: C) Many disliked it and called it ugly.
fields.option_d: D) They immediately made it a symbol of French pride.
fields.explanation: The passage states many Parisians disliked the tower at the time, calling it ugly.

fields.text:
Passage: 'Dolphins are highly social animals that live in groups called pods. They communicate with each other using clicks, whistles, and body movements. Dolphins are also known for their intelligence — they can recognize themselves in mirrors, solve puzzles, and learn from other dolphins.'

What is the main idea of this passage?
fields.option_a: A) Dolphins are dangerous to humans in the wild.
fields.option_b: B) Dolphins are social and intelligent animals.
fields.option_c: C) Dolphins are the fastest animals in the ocean.
fields.option_d: D) Dolphins only live in warm tropical waters.
fields.explanation: The passage describes dolphin social behavior and intelligence as its main focus.

fields.text:
A teacher recorded the test scores of her class after students used a new study guide. Before the study guide: average score = 72. After the study guide: average score = 85.

Which conclusion does the data best support?
fields.option_a: A) The study guide guaranteed every student would pass.
fields.option_b: B) Test scores improved after students used the study guide.
fields.option_c: C) The test became easier after the study guide was introduced.
fields.option_d: D) Students who used the study guide scored 100%.
fields.explanation: The average rose from 72 to 85 — directly showing improvement after the study guide was used.

fields.text:
A chart shows the number of books checked out from a school library each month. October: 320, November: 290, December: 180, January: 350.

In which month were the fewest books checked out?
fields.explanation: December had the lowest number at 180 checkouts.

fields.text:
Students were surveyed about their favorite school subject. Results: Math 35%, Science 28%, English 20%, History 17%.

Which subject was chosen by the fewest students?
fields.explanation: History had the lowest percentage at 17%.

fields.text:
The students in the classroom ________ quietly while the teacher handed out the exam.

Which verb correctly completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Students" is plural and past tense is needed. "Sat" is correct.

fields.text:
Every morning, she ________ her dog for a walk around the neighborhood.

Which verb correctly completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Every morning" signals a habitual present action. "Takes" is the correct simple present form for a singular subject.

fields.text:
The team ________ hard every day this week to prepare for the championship.

Which verb correctly completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "This week" with ongoing activity uses present perfect progressive: "has been practicing."

fields.text:
Neither of the two answers ________ correct.

Which verb correctly completes the sentence?
fields.explanation: "Neither" takes a singular verb: "is."

fields.text: Which sentence uses a period correctly?
fields.option_a: A) She finished her homework. Then she watched TV.
fields.option_b: B) She finished her homework, Then she watched TV.
fields.option_c: C) She finished her homework then. She watched TV.
fields.option_d: D) She finished. Her homework then watched TV.
